entry.summary: Nearly two-year investigation targets 23rd Street Gang in St. Lucie County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A nearly two-year investigation into the 23rd Street Gang has led to a law enforcement operation in St. Lucie County, the sheriff’s office said. Officials are expected to discuss the operation, criminal charges and the group’s alleged involvement in violent crimes and drug trafficking at a news conference Thursday. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said local, state and federal agencies took part in the investigation. The sheriff’s office, F ort Pierce Police Department , ATF , FBI , DEA , Florida Department of Law Enforcement , U.S. Marshals Service and Homeland Security Investigations were among the participating agencies. The sheriff’s office did not provide details about arrests or charges in its release. Officials scheduled a news conference for 2:30 p.m. Thursday at sheriff’s office headquarters. Sheriff Richard Del Toro , Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith and representatives from participating agencies are expected to speak. CBS12 previously reported on gang violence in the region, including a 2022 ride-along with St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office gang intelligence unit Detective Solomon Archie. Archie said Fort Pierce’s 23rd Street and 29th Street gangs operated on opposite sides of the area divided by 25th Street and Martin Luther King Jr. He also described gun violence as a major concern and said law enforcement agencies were working across county lines to identify suspects and respond to crime. In 2017, CBS12 also reported that the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office had launched a six-month crackdown on gangs and drugs in Fort Pierce. At that time, the sheriff said investigators focused on two violent gangs in Fort Pierce, the 10th Street gang and the 23rd Street gang. That operation resulted in more than five dozen arrests and 50 guns seized. The sheriff’s office said Thursday’s briefing will provide further details about the investigation and enforcement operation. CBS12 News will provide updates from the news conference later today.

entry.title: Judge rejects motion to dismiss animal cruelty case against Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo - WFLX
entry.summary: Judge rejects motion to dismiss animal cruelty case against Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo    WFLX
entry.article_text: A Martin County judge has denied a motion to dismiss the felony animal cruelty case against Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo, whose trial has been delayed at least nine times since her arrest more than two years ago. Prosecutor Kristen Chase confirmed to WFLX that Judge Elizabeth Metzger denied the defense’s second amended motion to dismiss during a 9 a.m. Camerlengo’s attorneys filed the motion, seeking to have the charges thrown out. Prosecutors opposed the request, filing a motion arguing the defense’s amended motion was “procedurally invalid and facially insufficient.” Wednesday’s ruling means the case against Camerlengo will continue, though a trial date has yet to be set. Camerlengo, the owner of Pawsitively Paradise in Palm City, was arrested in June 2024 on two felony animal cruelty charges after Martin County detectives said two dogs died while in her care. Her arrest followed a WFLX investigation that linked at least seven dog deaths or serious injuries to her training and boarding facility over the course of a decade. The latest ruling comes after more than two years of courtroom delays, disputes over expert witnesses and growing frustration from the judge overseeing the case. During a contentious July hearing , Metzger questioned both prosecutors and Camerlengo’s defense team about why the case had yet to go to trial. “I wanted you here, because I thought I was very clear in the past on what you needed to do,” Metzger said. “This case has been continued so many times, I’ve lost count.” In September, the trial was delayed for a ninth time after prosecutors told the court that a key witness was on medical disability and would be unable to testify until at least the end of January 2027. That witness must first testify at a hearing to determine whether she will be permitted to testify at trial. Camerlengo’s defense attorney, Stuart Kaplan, has also sought to exclude testimony from the Texas veterinary pathologist who performed necropsies on the two dogs and the lead detective who investigated their deaths. “I think the detective jumped the gun, so to speak. I don’t think she had all of the facts,” Kaplan previously told WFLX. Among those closely following the case is Adele Kirk Csontos, whose dog, Mako, died after spending approximately 48 hours at Pawsitively Paradise in November 2022. Kirk Csontos filed a police report following Mako’s death, but Camerlengo was never charged in connection with it because his necropsy was inconclusive. Necropsies of two other dogs determined they died from blunt force trauma, leading to Camerlengo’s arrest. “I mean, I know the wheels of justice turn very slowly, but no, I didn’t think it would be two years,” Kirk Csontos previously told WFLX. Despite the repeated delays, she said she remains hopeful. Believe it or not, I’m still hopeful that she will be held accountable,” she said. Camerlengo’s next court appearance, a docket sounding, is scheduled for Dec. No trial date has been announced.

entry.title: Family of Port St. Lucie teen killed walking to school raises concerns about road safety
entry.summary: WPTV hasn't stopped looking into the tragic death of a Port St. Lucie teen who was killed while walking to school just last month. On Wednesday, WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield sat down with the family for the first time to hear from them about their son and the questions they're still asking. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Family of 14-year old hit and killed by car in Port St. Lucie speak out  Jacory Brown, a freshman at Treasure Coast High School, was struck and killed by a car on Port St. Lucie Boulevard while walking to school early in the morning on Oct. 7. 'He just went to school,' Shelly-Ann Findley-Brown, mother, said. 'He was supposed to come back home. He didn't. His birthday would be on Monday. He would have been 15.' Findley-Brown, father Ainsworth Brown and grandfather Clovis Brown, sat down with WPTV. They're remembering Jacorys smile. 'He's kind, he's a jovial kid, said Findley-Brown. 'He's the life of our party of five.'  Theyre remembering his friendliness to others. '[He] was loved by so many persons, and he has touched everybody he's met,' Finely-Brown said.  And they're remembering his passion for entrepreneurship and graphic design like making cover art, business cards and flyers for friends and family. 'His hand was always up here, mind looking, his eyes all over like he's devising a plan and coming up with his thing,' Findley-Brown said.  But the family still has questions. They say Port St. Lucie Boulevard, with all the construction, makes it a dangerous roadway for kids walking to school. 'The road conditions are horrible,' Findley-Brown said. 'You are walking in puddles. And the night before, it rained. There was water all over the place. There's puddles. There's literally no sidewalks for kids to walk.' FDOT started construction back in 2025 to widen the road from two to four lanes and add new sidewalks and lights. But the project isn't expected to be completed until winter 2028. 'I hope the state takes this into a big consideration because it's not right walking to school when you don't have proper sidewalks,' Findley-Brown said. Jacory Brown will be laid to rest on Nov. 14. Friends have s tarted a GoFundMe to support the family.

entry.summary: 'Go Cats Go' is the name of the newly decorated JetBlue commercial plane revealed in Fort Lauderdale on Thursday. The 162-seat plane was shown to a group of media members, including WPTV Panthers anchor Mike Trim, at the Jetscape hangar at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. entry.title: Panthers Figure Skating Club member chases nationals berth with dreams of Team USA, Olympics
entry.summary: Several athletes with the Panthers Figure Skating Club are competing in the Eastern Sectional Finals this week in Boston, and for some skaters it's the final stop before nationals. One athlete competing is figure skater Skylar Zaglul. 'I'm really excited. I've worked really hard this whole year just for this moment, so I'm really looking forward to it,' Zaglul said. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Panthers figure skater chases Olympic dream 'I would definitely describe it as being harder than it looks,' Zaglul said. 'People look at the jumps and the spins like, wow, it's so impressive. It is, but a really hard part about it is also just the skating skills.' The 15-year-old said she trains six days a week a lot of practice to perfect her technique. 'I really love how skating brings out the toughness in me, and I just love how challenging it is,' Zaglul said. When asked what goes through her mind during a performance, she described her approach to staying present. 'I try to stay focused on one element at a time or else I can start thinking ahead too much, and it just goes,' Zaglul said. Zaglul is one of 30 high-performance skaters. The Panthers program has over 300 athletes in the figure skating club and 2,800 more kids in learn to skate. 'I love how I get to train alongside all my best friends,' Zaglul said. 'I think having good team bonding and my coaches, they're all what keeps me going,' Zaglul said. Asked about the end goal of her figure skating career, Zaglul pointed to the sport's highest stage. 'Well, I've always dreamed about being on Team USA. That's like something I've always wanted to do. Of course, being at the Olympics,' Zaglul said. Zaglul says her sights are set on the Olympics, but the first stop is getting to nationals. Her coaches and teammates tell me they'll be cheering her on the entire way.

entry.article_text: Nithya Raman, a little-known Los Angeles City Council member backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, has defeated Mayor Karen Bass, an upset that will alter the trajectory of the nation’s second-largest city.The India-born Raman's upstart campaign marked a generational shift at City Hall as voters followed the lead of New York, where democratic socialist Zohran Mamdani was elected last year. Raman, though, never attracted the same level of national attention and stressed her willingness to break with the progressive party at times during the campaign.Her entry into the race marked a stunning change of heart after she had initially endorsed Bass, once her ally. She said the city had reached a “breaking point” and announced her own candidacy just before the filing deadline.Bass said in a statement that she called Raman to congratulate her on her victory.“While this is not the outcome we hoped for, the people of Los Angeles have spoken,” Bass said. “I have committed to ensuring a smooth and seamless transition. Moving this city forward is what Los Angeles needs from all of us.”Bass becomes the first Los Angeles mayor in two decades to lose a bid for reelection. Her first term was undone by the deadly Palisades Fire, which ignited when she was out of the country and caught the fire department unprepared. The devastation left many voters with the unshakeable feeling that Bass should be held to account, and she never recovered.Raman's rise came in a year that saw Democratic divisions across the country, with insurgent left-wing candidates challenging establishment rivals.Raman is promising to oust the police chief, whom she views as too accommodating with federal immigration authorities. She also wants to improve basic services that have deteriorated for years and left neighborhoods with dirty, pothole-ridden streets, buckled sidewalks and broken streetlights.Raman called Bass’ efforts to reduce homelessness ineffective. She's promising a new approach on the crisis that would expand medical teams for people who live in encampments and on the streets in an effort to build trust and eventually bring them indoors. Raman also wants to provide more housing to move people out of hotels rented by the city for those who are homeless.She said her plans could reduce the number of people sleeping in tents and encampments by at least half by 2028, when the city will host the Olympic Games. However, the problem has long proved intractable, despite billions spent in the region.RELATED STORY | Keisha Lance Bottoms to become Georgia’s first Black governor, first woman governorRaman offered changeRaman, 45, was the face of change in a year when voters were restless over long-running problems that persisted under Bass, 73. A Berkeley IGS/LA Times poll conducted from Oct. 19 to 25 found that about 4 in 10 likely voters said reducing the number of homeless encampments should be a top priority for the next mayor to address, while about 3 in 10 said that about ensuring public safety or building more affordable housing.She was able to overcome criticism from Bass that she was “not ready for primetime” and too inexperienced to run a city with 3.8 million people, and she capitalized on anxiety over the future.“Our city is in crisis,” she said in one ad. The ad showed a lectern with no one behind it at the site of a massive warehouse fire from last summer, the homeless epicenter of Skid Row and shuttered malls and storefronts. “Where is our mayor?” Raman asked.Bass argued that she made enough progress to merit a second four-year term, and she branded Raman’s views on policing and homelessness as “extreme.”RELATED STORY | Xavier Becerra wins California gubernatorial race, making history as the state’s second Latino leaderTop Democrats lined up with BassRaman's victory came despite limited backing from the Democratic establishment. Bass had support from Gov. Gavin Newsom, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, along with nearly every member of the City Council. Bass served in the state Legislature and Congress before becoming mayor in 2022 and was under consideration to be former President Joe Biden’s running mate in 2020.In an important signal to the business community, billionaire developer Rick Caruso said he was voting for Bass, but stopped short of formally endorsing the candidate he lost to in the 2022 mayoral race.Raman, an urban planner, picked up notable support from advocacy and political groups, including Our Revolution, which was founded by Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders, and the Sierra Club. But she was thin on endorsements from prominent local politicians.She landed a widely publicized private meeting with former Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger, who was not involved in the race, that hinted at her efforts to broaden her circle. Expanding her network of allies could be crucial as she begins governing a city that's home to a struggling entertainment industry, a major port, world-class universities and research institutions and serves as a major tourist destination.

entry.title: Democrat clings to razor-thin lead in Mississippi Senate race
entry.summary: Mississippi voters could send a Democrat to the U.S. Senate for the first time in decades, with Scott Colom holding a narrow lead over Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. As of Thursday, Colom's lead over Hyde-Smith grew to more than 1,700 votes, with nearly 1 million ballots counted. In many states, a race this close would trigger an automatic recount. However, Mississippi has no law requiring automatic recounts in federal elections. Instead, a court would have to order one. RELATED STORY | 2026 midterm election results: Key races for Senate, House and governor The race remains too close to call, with as many as 3,500 mail-in ballots still outstanding, according to the Mississippi secretary of state's office. Mississippi allows mail-in ballots to arrive after Election Day as long as they are postmarked by Election Day. However, not all outstanding ballots are necessarily expected to arrive, as some voters who requested ballots may not have returned them. In addition to mail-in ballots, election officials must review provisional ballots, known in Mississippi as affidavit ballots. Voters may cast affidavit ballots for several reasons, including failing to present identification at the polls. Those voters must provide the required identification to county election officials after Election Day for their ballots to count. Other affidavit ballots may have been cast by voters listed as inactive on the state's voter rolls. Those ballots can be counted once officials confirm the voters' eligibility through the state's registration system, without requiring additional action from the voters. Counties have until Nov. 13 to submit their certified election results to the Mississippi secretary of state's office, meaning an official winner may not be determined for several more days. Mississippi has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1982.

entry.title: Nearly two-year investigation targets 23rd Street Gang in St. Lucie County - WPEC
entry.summary: Nearly two-year investigation targets 23rd Street Gang in St. Lucie County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A nearly two-year investigation into the 23rd Street gang has led to nearly 40 arrests and the seizure of guns, drugs and cash, law enforcement officials said Thursday. The multi-agency investigation, called Operation Score Board, focused on alleged gang activity in northwest Fort Pierce and surrounding areas. Officials said investigators linked 13 people to an alleged criminal conspiracy involving fraud, drug trafficking, shootings and homicides. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said investigators reviewed 10 years of criminal activity and connected people associated with the gang to nearly 100 shootings. Investigators also found that gang members allegedly kept a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, which inspired the operation’s name. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said local, state and federal agencies took part in the investigation. The sheriff’s office, F ort Pierce Police Department , ATF , FBI , DEA , Florida Department of Law Enforcement , U.S. Marshals Service and Homeland Security Investigations were among the participating agencies. Officials said about 70 to 80 people are documented as members of the gang. The investigation focused on people police described as shot callers who allegedly directed its activities. Authorities said the 23rd Street gang has been a problem in the Fort Pierce area for decades and was the most violent of several gangs in the city. 4, officers served five search warrants four in Fort Pierce and one in Port St. Lucie beginning around 5 a.m. The operation led to 11 arrests on racketeering charges, with two people still wanted on warrants, and four additional probable-cause arrests, officials said. Authorities said some people connected to the investigation had already been arrested during its earlier stages. 4 searches yielded seven firearms, about one pound of marijuana, 15 grams of cocaine, 50 grams of MDMA and $18,474. Across the investigation, police said they seized 18 firearms, 20 pounds of marijuana, 532 grams of cocaine and two grams of MDPV. Authorities did not identify the people they believe led the gang, but said they believe they have arrested most of the key players. They said some people connected to the investigation have faced murder charges, but declined to discuss active cases. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro called the operation an unusually large collaboration among local, state and federal agencies. He said investigators took significant players off the streets and that more operations are expected. The sheriff said the case took extensive work to connect years of records and evidence, and involved a 2,000-page report and a 150-page affidavit. Officials also credited the State Attorney’s Office with helping build the case. History of problems CBS12 previously reported on gang violence in the region, including a 2022 ride-along with St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office gang intelligence unit Detective Solomon Archie. Archie said Fort Pierce’s 23rd Street and 29th Street gangs operated on opposite sides of the area divided by 25th Street and Martin Luther King Jr. He also described gun violence as a major concern and said law enforcement agencies were working across county lines to identify suspects and respond to crime. In 2017, CBS12 also reported that the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office had launched a six-month crackdown on gangs and drugs in Fort Pierce. At that time, the sheriff said investigators focused on two violent gangs in Fort Pierce, the 10th Street gang and the 23rd Street gang. That operation resulted in more than five dozen arrests and 50 guns seized. The sheriff’s office said Thursday’s briefing will provide further details about the investigation and enforcement operation. CBS12 News will provide updates from the news conference later today.

entry.title: Judge rejects motion to dismiss animal cruelty case against Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo - WFLX
entry.summary: Judge rejects motion to dismiss animal cruelty case against Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo    WFLX
entry.article_text: A Martin County judge has denied a motion to dismiss the felony animal cruelty case against Palm City dog trainer Nikki Camerlengo, whose trial has been delayed at least nine times since her arrest more than two years ago. Prosecutor Kristen Chase confirmed to WFLX that Judge Elizabeth Metzger denied the defense’s second amended motion to dismiss during a 9 a.m. Camerlengo’s attorneys filed the motion, seeking to have the charges thrown out. Prosecutors opposed the request, filing a motion arguing the defense’s amended motion was “procedurally invalid and facially insufficient.” Wednesday’s ruling means the case against Camerlengo will continue, though a trial date has yet to be set. Camerlengo, the owner of Pawsitively Paradise in Palm City, was arrested in June 2024 on two felony animal cruelty charges after Martin County detectives said two dogs died while in her care. Her arrest followed a WFLX investigation that linked at least seven dog deaths or serious injuries to her training and boarding facility over the course of a decade. The latest ruling comes after more than two years of courtroom delays, disputes over expert witnesses and growing frustration from the judge overseeing the case. During a contentious July hearing , Metzger questioned both prosecutors and Camerlengo’s defense team about why the case had yet to go to trial. “I wanted you here, because I thought I was very clear in the past on what you needed to do,” Metzger said. “This case has been continued so many times, I’ve lost count.” In September, the trial was delayed for a ninth time after prosecutors told the court that a key witness was on medical disability and would be unable to testify until at least the end of January 2027. That witness must first testify at a hearing to determine whether she will be permitted to testify at trial. Camerlengo’s defense attorney, Stuart Kaplan, has also sought to exclude testimony from the Texas veterinary pathologist who performed necropsies on the two dogs and the lead detective who investigated their deaths. “I think the detective jumped the gun, so to speak. I don’t think she had all of the facts,” Kaplan previously told WFLX. Among those closely following the case is Adele Kirk Csontos, whose dog, Mako, died after spending approximately 48 hours at Pawsitively Paradise in November 2022. Kirk Csontos filed a police report following Mako’s death, but Camerlengo was never charged in connection with it because his necropsy was inconclusive. Necropsies of two other dogs determined they died from blunt force trauma, leading to Camerlengo’s arrest. “I mean, I know the wheels of justice turn very slowly, but no, I didn’t think it would be two years,” Kirk Csontos previously told WFLX. Despite the repeated delays, she said she remains hopeful. Believe it or not, I’m still hopeful that she will be held accountable,” she said. Camerlengo’s next court appearance, a docket sounding, is scheduled for Dec. No trial date has been announced.

entry.title: New reimagined Florida Panthers JetBlue plane debuts in Fort Lauderdale
entry.summary: 'Go Cats Go' is the name of the newly decorated JetBlue commercial plane revealed in Fort Lauderdale on Thursday. The 162-seat plane was shown to a group of media members, including WPTV Panthers anchor Mike Trim, at the Jetscape hangar at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. WATCH REPORT BELOW: JetBlue unveils Florida Panthers-themed plane 'You guys see my new plane?' joked Panthers star forward Brad Marchand. Marchand was joined at the ceremony by Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov and Panthers General Manager Bill Zito. The commercial airliner is capable of flying to all 130 JetBlue destinations and will fly locally out of South Florida, including Donald J. Trump International Airport. 'There's an energy from it. It's so beautiful. It's so cool, and I'm already proud of it, and I really have no reason to be proud of it. It's just really special and really cool,' said Zito. The plane features Panthers logos old and new. The current Panthers shield is featured on the tail while the classic jumping cat logo is on the underbelly. Marchand, Barkov and Zito added a special touch at the ceremony by signing the jumping cat logo with Sharpies. For Barkov, it's another step in seeing the Panthers brand grow. 'I love it. It's been fun to see this community grow, get more and more fans, more and more involved in here, and just seeing Florida Panthers everywhere. You see it on the highways, you see like, everywhere and now this plane,' said Barkov. The plane's first flight will be to Boston on Thursday, home of the rival Bruins. Marchand captained that team for years and told Trim and a group of reporters, 'I almost feel like they might have done that on purpose. You know, because it's not a plane that you're going to miss. It all stands out. They did an incredible job with it.'  Representatives from JetBlue told Trim the plane's Panthers livery will stay for at least five years.

entry.title: FAU men's basketball replaces nearly entire roster but welcomes highest-rated recruit in school history
entry.summary: It's a new season for the FAU Owls basketball team, with a lot of new faces, including the school's highest-rated recruit in school history, Felipe Quinones. 'I'm just grateful to play at a level I could only dream of playing at,' said Quinones, a 6-foot-4, four-star recruit who impresses in transition and can simply put the ball in the basket. WATCH REPORT BELOW: FAU men's basketball rebuilds roster, welcomes highest-rated recruit in school history 'It's a dream come true, and I'm living my dream right now, so it's easy and fun. This is what I always wanted to do,' Quinones said. At this point of the season, FAU stands 1-0 after a 14-point win on Monday against LIU. We got a young team, but we're all learning each other and getting better,' said senior guard Kanaan Carlyle, who's the lone returner from last year's squad, and in his senior year, hes not taking anything for granted. 'I love it. Thats the reason I chose to come back. I got a great staff and great teammates,' Carlyle said. While Carlyle is the coach on the court, John Jakus is the coach of the team, now in his third year. After going 18-15 last season, Jakus was building momentum, but he lost nearly his entire roster. Now, hes starting over and embracing the challenge. 'We're in a great spot, and we're grateful to be able to start with a win and mix in first-year students with transfers. We're just trying to get a little healthy with two of our guards, but well get there, Jakus said.

entry.summary: Flooding leaves Creekside community in St. Lucie County without power, most homes evacuated    WFLX
entry.article_text: Floodwaters remain knee-deep in parts of the Creekside community in St. Lucie County, where officials say roughly 75% of the neighborhood's homes have been evacuated, and power remains shut off. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro provided a Thursday update , saying the community, located off State Road 70 west of Florida's Turnpike, has about 150 homes and remains under a voluntary evacuation. WATCH AERIAL VIDEO OF THE FLOODING: Del Toro said some trucks can now make it into the neighborhood, but water levels remain high. Lucie County Sheriff's Office also has a high-water vehicle available to assist residents who need help. "If in fact you need help, please don't hesitate to call 911 or contact one of our deputies," Del Toro said. Deputies are providing 24-hour security in the community while residents remain displaced and electricity is out, according to the sheriff. Restoring power could take additional time because some of Florida Power Light's equipment remains underwater. "We continue to monitor the water level just like everybody else," FPL's Marshall Critchfield said. "Much of our equipment is presently underwater and our priority number one, as always, is safety." Critchfield said crews will restore electricity as soon as water recedes enough for them to safely access the equipment. Del Toro said the neighborhood has underground utilities, creating an additional challenge while flooding remains high. Officials did not provide an estimate for when power would be restored or when the water is expected to fully recede. Del Toro urged residents who need assistance to contact deputies or call 911.

entry.title: Six St. Lucie County polling places moved because of flooding on Election Day - WPEC
entry.summary: Six St. Lucie County polling places moved because of flooding on Election Day    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie County election officials to move six precincts’ polling places on Election Day, including several in Port St. The Supervisor of Elections Office announced the changes in a notice posted Monday. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker said inclement weather and flooding affected road access to some voting sites. The office said the moves are meant to give voters safe and accessible locations to cast their ballots. Lucie, voters in precincts 49 and 71, who normally cast ballots at Oak Hammock K-8 School, will vote at the Port St. Lucie Community Center at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd. Precinct 51 voters, who normally vote at the Disabled American Veterans Hall, will also go to the community center. The county says voters should enter from Airoso Boulevard. Voters in precincts 67 and 86 will not vote at Centennial High School in St. They will vote at Indian River State College’s Veterans Center of Excellence, at 500 NW California Blvd. The county says access is from Peacock Boulevard. See also: Inside David Jolly's election night watch party as Florida chooses its next governor In the Tradition area, precinct 83 voters will move from the Paula A. Lewis Library to Tradition Town Hall at 10799 SW Civic Ln. Precinct 92 voters will also move from The Brennity at Tradition to Tradition Town Hall. In Fort Pierce, Precinct 12 voters will move from the Fort Pierce Masonic Lodge to the Days Inn Midtown at 3224 S US Highway 1. The notice does not list any polling places as closed. It also does not say whether voters who already went to their normal location will be redirected on site. The flooding also disrupted schools. Lucie Public Schools Superintendent Jon Prince apologized to families during a news conference Tuesday, after students were seen walking through standing water to get home Monday. We didn’t anticipate anything like what transpired yesterday. Caused a lot of stress for our families, and for that, I’m profoundly sorry, Prince said. Schools are closed Wednesday. Prince said the district expects to reopen Thursday if roads are clear, and that no school buildings took significant water. A private security company that patrols homeowners associations in the Tradition area joined the rescue effort with high-water vehicles. TACT Tech Security CEO Taylor Matchton said his crews lifted elderly residents into a Jeep after water rose waist-high in one community. We had no goal when we came out here. We had just ambition to figure out how we can help anyone and anywhere and do whatever we can with the resources that we have, Matchton said. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said deputies would work extra shifts overnight, especially in evacuated neighborhoods, and warned that anyone who preys on flood victims will face zero tolerance. The sheriff said there was no playbook for a storm like this. But the most important thing is we’re all working together with one purpose, which is to serve this community, Del Toro said. The county opened a general shelter at Northport K-8 School. Principal Brie Lamb said the campus stayed dry and has cots, blankets, meals, and coffee. Anybody who may need a place tonight, please come in, Lamb said. Officials said about 14 or 15 people were staying there at the time of the briefing. County leaders said it could take up to seven days for conditions to return to normal. The National Weather Service flood warning for St. Lucie County remains in effect until 9:30 a.m. Officials ask residents to stay home if they can and to call 911 only for life-threatening emergencies Voters with questions can call the Supervisor of Elections Office at 772-462-1500 or visit stlucievotes.gov .

entry.title: Amendment 3 promises property tax savings, but Florida cities now face tough budget choices
entry.summary: The passing of Amendment 3 has now put Florida cities on notice to find ways to handle the anticipated loss of revenue. 'I was interviewed a couple of years ago when this first came up, and I said, 'What are we going to do, have a bake sale,' and here we are,' says Lake Worth Beach Mayor Betty Resch. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Florida Cities Chart Uncertain Future Under Amendment 3 According to Florida Tax Watch, Lake Worth Beach stands to lose $2.9 million in the first year of the higher homestead exemption and $5 million in the second year. 'We can't just keep raising the fees. We can't charge somebody if they want to go to the library,' Resch said. Voters made a statement on affordability, with 62% approving the referendum. The measure raises the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, which will mean savings on property tax bills. Local governments that depend on property tax revenue now face tightening budgets by making cuts, reducing services and possibly finding new ways to raise revenue. 'We don't charge yet for parking downtown, and every time we talk about it, everybody flips out because they don't want it and neither do I,' Resch said. 'I don't know where we're going to go. I don't know what we're going to do.'

entry.title: NTSB recovers part of Learjet engine, asks public to report crash debris
entry.summary: Investigators have recovered a portion of an engine from the Learjet 60 that crashed near Greenacres on Sunday as crews continue excavating the crash site, according to the National Transportation Safety Board. The NTSB said excavation work began late Wednesday and continued Thursday as investigators and local officials worked to recover wreckage from the crash that killed nine people. Debris from the aircraft has been found away from the main impact site, including on the roofs of nearby homes and buildings, according to the NTSB. All recovered wreckage will be taken to a secure location for further examination. Investigators are also asking residents who find debris believed to be from the Learjet not to keep it or attempt to move, alter or dispose of it. The agency said even small pieces of wreckage could contain evidence that helps investigators determine what happened. Anyone who has found or collected debris from the crash is asked to email witness@ntsb.gov to arrange for its recovery. The NTSB is asking people to include a photograph of the debris in the email, if possible. The NTSB said recovering as much of the aircraft wreckage as possible is critical to its investigation and efforts to determine the cause of the crash.

entry.title: Washington Elementary in Palm Beach County to remain closed Friday due to flooding conditions
entry.summary: Washington Elementary School in Palm Beach County will remain closed Friday as severe flooding and dangerous conditions continue to affect parts of the community, according to the school district. All other schools operated by the School District of Palm Beach County will be open Friday, Chief of Communications Sean Cooley said. The district said its priority is reopening schools only when it is safe to do so, acknowledging that some neighborhoods continue to experience severe flooding that could make travel difficult or dangerous. Families and staff members who cannot safely get to school are being urged not to put themselves at risk. Any student absences caused by weather-related impacts will be fully excused through Friday, according to the district. 'Our top priority is reopening schools only when it is safe to do so,' the district said. Greg Abbott in favor of Democrat Gina Hinojosa.RELATED STORY | 2026 midterm election results: Key races for Senate, House and governorThe biggest share of Musk's Texas spending moved in two checks in September. According to the Senate Leadership Fund's third-quarter Federal Election Commission report, Musk gave the main Senate Republican super PAC $75 million on Sept. 9 and another $83 million on Sept. 23.The day after each donation, the fund transferred the exact same amount to Texas PAC, a super PAC supporting Paxton. The filings don't prove Musk's specific dollars funded those transfers, but the timing drew wide attention.Musk also gave Abbott $5 million in the final stretch of the race, according to state campaign finance filings first reported by Politico. The $474 million total runs only through mid-October. Post-election FEC reports due Dec. 3 will show whether he gave more in the campaign's final weeks.For Musk, the spending is a small slice of his fortune. With a net worth estimated at roughly $875 billion, the $474 million amounts to about 0.05% of his wealth. That's roughly the equivalent of someone with $400,000 to their name spending $200, according to a Scripps News calculation.Texas has become the home base for Musk's business empire. He began moving operations there in 2020 after clashing with California over pandemic restrictions at Tesla's factory in the state.Today, Tesla runs its largest U.S. vehicle factory outside Austin, and SpaceX launches rockets from its Starbase complex in South Texas. In August, SpaceX and Tesla picked Grimes County for Terafab, a chip manufacturing complex projected to cost $55 billion in its first phase and up to $119 billion in total.Those operations rely heavily on state decisions about electricity, water, environmental permits, infrastructure and tax incentives. Abbott had been a vocal supporter of Musk's projects, and Paxton's office had largely avoided scrutinizing Musk's companies even as it took on other Big Tech firms.Talarico made the flood of outside money part of his message on election night."We went up against all the negative ads, smear campaigns, foreign bots, and AI deepfakes that money can buy," Talarico said. "They played dirty because they were desperate. And against big money and long odds, we took our power back."IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Trump deflects blame for Republican midterm losses as finger-pointing beginsInvestors reacted quickly. SpaceX shares closed down 3.8% on Wednesday and Tesla fell 3.3%, even as the broader market rose, and are tracking even further drops during market trading Thursday.Musk responded on X with a nod to one of his newer ventures: "Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now."Hinojosa inherits the office that oversaw more than $1.6 billion in tax incentives for Musk's companies. She campaigned against generous corporate subsidies and has promised to freeze new data center approvals until the Legislature puts protections in place.Her campaign has said Terafab alone received about $1.7 billion in school tax exemptions. entry.title: Guns, drugs and lots of money: 40 arrested in major Fort Pierce gang takedown - WPBF
entry.summary: Guns, drugs and lots of money: 40 arrested in major Fort Pierce gang takedown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Law enforcement officials in St. Lucie County announced Thursday that 40 suspected members of a Fort Pierce gang have been arrested following an 18-month investigation. The investigation, known as "Operation Score Board," targeted the 23rd Street Gang, which authorities say has operated in northern St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the gang has between 70 and 80 members and has been responsible for years of violence in the Fort Pierce community. "This gang has terrorized, basically created a hostage crisis for our community up there," Del Toro said. "There’s a lot of good people that are up there in Fort Pierce that have been just held hostage by this group for the last decade, living in fear." Investigators said the gang even maintained a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, a discovery that ultimately gave the operation its name. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said detectives reviewed a decade of criminal activity to identify connections between suspected gang members and violent crimes. "Detectives conducted an extensive review of criminal activity spanning ten years, examining incidents and identifying connections between individuals associated with the gang," Smith said. "This intensive analysis revealed a disturbing pattern of organized crime and violence." Authorities said investigators used Florida’s RICO law to connect years of alleged shootings, drug trafficking and other criminal activity to members of the 23rd Street Gang. The investigation involved multiple local and state law enforcement agencies working together over 18 months to build cases against suspected members of the organization. On Wednesday, law enforcement officers executed multiple search warrants throughout the Fort Pierce area, resulting in 11 arrests as part of the larger operation. Authorities said officers also seized multiple firearms, drugs and thousands of dollars in cash. Del Toro said the size of the operation and the cooperation between agencies could have a lasting impact on the community. "I’ve never seen an operation this large with this many agencies at the local and federal level," Del Toro said. "I think this is going to have a significant generational impact in this community." Authorities said similar investigations and operations are expected in the future. entry.title: 23rd Street gang investigation leads to nearly 40 arrests in St. Lucie County - WPEC
entry.summary: 23rd Street gang investigation leads to nearly 40 arrests in St. Lucie County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A nearly two-year investigation into the 23rd Street gang has led to nearly 40 arrests and the seizure of guns, drugs and cash, law enforcement officials said Thursday. The multi-agency investigation, called Operation Score Board, focused on alleged gang activity in northwest Fort Pierce and surrounding areas. Officials said investigators linked 13 people to an alleged criminal conspiracy involving fraud, drug trafficking, shootings and homicides. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said investigators reviewed 10 years of criminal activity and connected people associated with the gang to nearly 100 shootings. Investigators also found that gang members allegedly kept a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, which inspired the operation’s name. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said local, state and federal agencies took part in the investigation. The sheriff’s office, F ort Pierce Police Department , ATF , FBI , DEA , Florida Department of Law Enforcement , U.S. Marshals Service and Homeland Security Investigations were among the participating agencies. "Hundreds of shootings over the last decade, violent crime terrorizing the north end of this county, and our community deserves better, and they're getting better because of the hard work of the men and women with the special investigation units that the chief mentioned, and our federal partners here," said Sheriff Richard Del Toro. Officials said about 70 to 80 people are documented as members of the gang. The investigation focused on people police described as shot callers who allegedly directed its activities. Authorities said the 23rd Street gang has been a problem in the Fort Pierce area for decades and was the most violent of several gangs in the city. 4, officers served five search warrants four in Fort Pierce and one in Port St. Lucie beginning around 5 a.m. The operation led to 11 arrests on racketeering charges, with two people still wanted on warrants, and four additional probable-cause arrests, officials said. Authorities said some people connected to the investigation had already been arrested during its earlier stages. 4 searches yielded seven firearms, about one pound of marijuana, 15 grams of cocaine, 50 grams of MDMA and $18,474. Across the investigation, police said they seized 18 firearms, 20 pounds of marijuana, 532 grams of cocaine and two grams of MDPV. "We remain committed to identifying, investigating, and holding accountable those responsible for bringing violence and criminal activity into our neighborhoods," Chief Smith said. "Our message is clear: We will not tolerate organized criminal activity that threatens the safety of our residents." Authorities did not identify the people they believe led the gang, but said they believe they have arrested most of the key players. They said some people connected to the investigation have faced murder charges, but declined to discuss active cases. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro called the operation an unusually large collaboration among local, state and federal agencies. He said investigators took significant players off the streets and that more operations are expected. The sheriff said the case took extensive work to connect years of records and evidence, and involved a 2,000-page report and a 150-page affidavit. Officials also credited the State Attorney’s Office with helping build the case. History of problems CBS12 previously reported on gang violence in the region, including a 2022 ride-along with St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office gang intelligence unit Detective Solomon Archie. Archie said Fort Pierce’s 23rd Street and 29th Street gangs operated on opposite sides of the area divided by 25th Street and Martin Luther King Jr. He also described gun violence as a major concern and said law enforcement agencies were working across county lines to identify suspects and respond to crime. In 2017, CBS12 also reported that the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office had launched a six-month crackdown on gangs and drugs in Fort Pierce. At that time, the sheriff said investigators focused on two violent gangs in Fort Pierce, the 10th Street gang and the 23rd Street gang. That operation resulted in more than five dozen arrests and 50 guns seized.

entry.title: William T. Dwyer looks to secure their second straight golf championship
entry.summary: Two years ago, when William T. Dwyer hired Head Golf Coach Eric Fasone, his goal was simple. Our vision was to create a strong program here at Dwyer for boys golf, said Fasone. In year one, the fellas went undefeated and won state, and this year, We went through our regular season with only one loss, and we swept our tournaments, said Fasone. This year, their star is the stellar senior TK Ritthisorn. It wasnt really nerves we knew we were good you know we know our players and we just went out there and did our best and dominated other teams, said Ritthisorn, who was named the district's most outstanding player. It was pretty hard; I played my game and flighted shots and knew what I was doing and I just dominated and played my best, said Ritthisorn. While hes the only returner from last year's championship squad, hes not the only star on the team; in fact theyre team captain is Drew Politziner, who spent the entire season daring his guys to be great. I was very honored that coach gave me the option to be the captain this year for the team and the leadership I give is really overal what Dwyer stands for, said Politziner. With his leadership, TKs clutch skills, and some new faces like Cole Mitchell and Drew Kiernan, the boys swept through districts, sectionals, and regionals. Going into districts I knew we were supposed to win it again and regionals I didnt really know much about the course, said Mitchell. We got the Mamba Mentality, so were supposed to go out and win every single match and do the best we can, said Kiernan. That Mamba mentality has the fellas headed to the state Tournament this weekend, a moment the guys have been waiting on. Im excited to see what everyone can do and play their best, and no matter how hard it is, everyone will do their part,' said junior Tyler Sheehan.

entry.title: 'It's still rising': Jensen Beach homes flooded - WPTV
entry.summary: 'It's still rising': Jensen Beach homes flooded    WPTV
entry.article_text: Much of a Jensen Beach neighborhood on Hyline Drive is underwater after this week's heavy rain overwhelmed the local drainage system. As of Wednesday afternoon, water levels inside some homes are still rising long after the rain stopped.For Lisa French and Tiffany Kincaid, a kayak has become the way to get around their flooded community.WATCH REPORT BELOW: At Kincaid's home, the water level is waist-deep."We're currently taking stuff out of our house right now, salvaging what we can," said Kincaid.At French's home, the damage has just begun, with the water level climbing to 4 inches deep."My floorboards are outside, but it's still rising. My husband made a mark inside so it's still coming up and ours isn't nearly as bad as everyone else," French said.Their homes are among dozens in the neighborhood under water after Monday's heavy rain saturated the ground and inundated the drainage system."We were expecting flooding to go down. Clearly drainage is not — things are not draining correctly," Kincaid said.Martin County told us the neighborhood is uniquely located next to the Savannas Preserve, where water is naturally flowing south from other areas that flooded. For now, the county says it's unable to pump water out of the community because the nearby watershed doesn't have capacity, but relief may be on the horizon."As the water level drops, that's going to drain the ponds that we need to pump into, and that's going to allow us to do that," Martin County's Public Works Director Jim Gordon said. "We're maximizing what we can downstream, and we might see it trending in the right direction."Residents are hoping relief comes sooner rather than later so they can start the long road to recovery."Even after, like, our houses are wrecked," French said."It's just a lot to take in right now for us," Kincaid said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: Vero Beach police seek help identifying four people in hotel damage investigation    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Vero Beach police are asking for the public's help identifying four people accused of damaging a hotel room door and door frame at the Islander Inn. According to the Vero Beach Police Department , the incident happened around 12:59 a.m. 1 at the hotel, located at 3101 Ocean Drive. Investigators said surveillance footage captured four individuals at the property. Witnesses reported hearing loud banging or kicking noises before discovering damage to a room's door and door frame. Polie released surveillance images of the individuals as part of an effort to identify them. The department classified the incident as criminal mischief. See also: Resources for residents and business owners after heavy rain and flooding Anyone who recognizes the individuals or has information about the incident is asked to contact Detective Fonseca with the Vero Beach Police Department at 772-978-4667 or by email at gfonseca@vbpd.org. People wishing to remain anonymous can contact Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. Tipsters may be eligible for a cash reward. The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.title: Palm Beach County flooding prompts questions about drainage, development and emergency response

The declaration gives state and local officials additional authority and resources for response, recovery and mitigation efforts. The declaration gives state and local officials additional authority and resources for response, recovery and mitigation efforts.County commissioners are now weighing in on the flooding and what they’ve seen in their communities."This rain, my gosh, it never ends," Commissioner Maria Sachs said.Commissioner Gregg Weiss pointed to the extraordinary rainfall totals in parts of West Palm Beach."Parts of West Palm Beach received over 22 inches of rain," Weiss said. "These were epic amounts of water that came down very quickly."Weiss described the rainfall as the kind of extreme event some characterize as a "one-in-1,000-type" storm. He also acknowledged that some residents will be dealing with the consequences long after the rain stops."I know in some of our eastern areas their homes received water inside, so there’s going to be work to do there," Weiss said.For Sachs, the flooding is also raising a larger question about how Palm Beach County prepares for future growth.She pointed to the importance of planning for drainage when new homes and businesses are built."I know our aquifers can take only so much," Sachs said. "When we develop residences and commercial properties, we develop them with the idea of drainage."The flooding has turned roads into waterways, stranded vehicles and left some residents unable to get out of their neighborhoods.Among those who were affected was Commissioner Bobby Powell Jr., who represents Palm Beach County Commission District 7."There's people in my community that were not able to go to work," Powell said.Powell told commissioners that he experienced the flooding firsthand."Fire Rescue came to get me this morning, so I'm one of the people they had to rescue," Powell said.Palm Beach County Fire Rescue told WPTV its crews conducted multiple flood response operations from Sunday through Tuesday.Sunday night, firefighters responded to more than seventy 911 calls in the Century Village area near West Palm Beach. Nearly 100 residents were trapped in stranded vehicles as floodwaters rapidly rose.WATCH BELOW: Flooding in Century VillageFirefighters reported encountering floating cars with people still inside and water reaching between 3 and 4 feet deep in some areas.Crews deployed drones equipped with thermal imaging cameras around Century Village, Cypress Lakes, the Tennis Club and other areas to search vehicles for people who needed help.Firefighters then waded through the water and used high-water vehicles and brush trucks to rescue residents and bring them to higher ground.Fire Rescue said there were no injuries during those operations.Palm Beach County Fire Rescue's Urban Search and Rescue Swiftwater Response Team was also deployed to Riviera Beach for nearly 24 hours.With some streets impassable, rescue specialists used emergency rafts and boats to go door to door.Fire Rescue said its teams:Evacuated 71 peopleConducted two medical rescuesEvacuated nine petsCounty officials have continued reporting significant impacts from the flooding in Riviera Beach and other communities.PBCFR said from Nov. 1-3, crews responded to a total of more than 1,600 emergency calls across the county. This figure included all 911 calls, not just flooding.The flooding wasn't the only major emergency stretching Palm Beach County's resources.At the same time, fire rescue crews were carrying out flood response operations; dozens of personnel and resources were also dedicated to the deadly Learjet crash near Greenacres.The crash also displaced an estimated 400 to 600 people from a nearby mobile home community. WPTV spoke with residents who were unable to return to their homes, vehicles and belongings while investigators worked through the crash scene.The county then opened an emergency shelter where some residents have been ever since."We've been communicating with our municipalities, making sure we have shelters, that we have anything needed to address the concerns of our families," said Commissioner Joel Flores, adding Election Day presented another challenge as he noted three precincts had to be moved because of all the flooding.Vice Mayor Marci Woodward pointed to the strain of responding to both disasters at once."We had a horrific plane crash and also ended up with flooding, so to all the employees that have worked a lot of long hours, I wanted to personally thank all of you, and I know our residents appreciate all the efforts, so thank you for that," Woodward said.State of emergency now includes Palm Beach CountyThe county’s response is continuing with the state now involved in recovery efforts.DeSantis amended Florida's existing flooding emergency order Wednesday to add Palm Beach County along with Glades, Hendry, Lake, Okeechobee, Seminole and Volusia counties.The Florida Division of Emergency Management said the move strengthens the state's ability to deploy resources, support local response efforts and help communities recover.The emergency declaration also gives state and local officials additional authority to carry out response, recovery and mitigation efforts, including logistical, rescue and evacuation operations. Local governments can waive certain procedures involving public works, contracts, equipment, workers and spending when necessary to speed up the emergency response.If you're in need of flooding emergency, call 2-1-1.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: NTSB recovers part of Learjet engine, asks public to report crash debris
entry.summary: Investigators have recovered a portion of an engine from the Learjet 60 that crashed near Greenacres on Sunday as crews continue excavating the crash site, according to the National Transportation Safety Board. The NTSB said excavation work began late Wednesday and continued Thursday as investigators and local officials worked to recover wreckage from the crash that killed nine people. WATCH BELOW: Piece of jet's tail found miles away NTSB: Piece of Learjet's tail found miles away from crash Debris from the aircraft has been found away from the main impact site, including on the roofs of nearby homes and buildings, according to the NTSB. All recovered wreckage will be taken to a secure location for further examination. Investigators are also asking residents who find debris believed to be from the Learjet not to keep it or attempt to move, alter or dispose of it. The agency said even small pieces of wreckage could contain evidence that helps investigators determine what happened. Anyone who has found or collected debris from the crash is asked to email witness@ntsb.gov to arrange for its recovery. The NTSB is asking people to include a photograph of the debris in the email, if possible. The NTSB said recovering as much of the aircraft wreckage as possible is critical to its investigation and efforts to determine the cause of the crash.

entry.summary: St. Lucie, Indian River County schools to remain closed Friday    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Public schools in Indian River and St. Lucie counties will remain closed Friday, Nov. 6, with both districts planning to reopen Monday, Nov. 9, as flooding continues to affect transportation and access to some campuses. In Indian River County, the school district cited limited bus driver availability and significant delays along County Roads 510 and 512. School buildings will be accessible to instructional staff preparing for Monday’s return. Activities and extracurriculars are scheduled to resume Thursday, Nov. Additionally, the Palm Beach County School District announced that Washington Elementary School will remain closed Friday. Lucie County, the district said flooding has left some bus stops and roads inaccessible and affected access to some campuses. Some families and employees also remain without power or cannot safely leave their neighborhoods. Lucie Public Schools canceled athletics through Sunday, Nov. Athletic activities may resume Monday. The SAT scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 7, has been rescheduled for Nov. See also: 'Up to my chest': Family raises concerns after 7-year-old walks through deep floodwaters Five Boys & Girls Clubs locations in St. Lucie County will be open from 8 a.m. for current members and anyone interested in joining. Each site can accommodate up to 100 members, who may attend any location. Families can register at bgcofslc.org . Children should bring a packed lunch, snack and water bottle. The locations are: Chuck Hill, 198 Marion Ave., Port St. Jenkins Road, Fort Pierce Ken Pruitt, 10673 SE Lennard Road, Port St. Lucie Percy Peek Teen, 2902 Avenue D, Fort Pierce Garden Terrace, 3104 Avenue J, Fort Pierce The St. Lucie County district said it will share information about any required instructional make-up days when available. Both districts said they will continue monitoring conditions and sharing updates through their official channels.

entry.title: GOP meltdown sparks battle over who's to blame
entry.summary: Even as key Senate races remain unresolved in Mississippi and Alaska, Republicans have already begun searching for someone to blame after a devastating midterm election defeat. With Democrats securing control of the Senate and on track for major gains in the House, the conversation in Washington has quickly shifted from counting ballots to assigning responsibility. The outstanding races remain extraordinarily close. In Mississippi, just over 1,000 votes separate the candidates, with additional mail ballots still eligible to arrive under state law. Alaska's contest may take even longer to resolve because of its ranked-choice voting system, where second- and third-choice preferences could ultimately determine the winner. But while election officials continue tallying votes, Republicans are increasingly focused on what many in the party view as one of the worst electoral setbacks in decades. RELATED STORY | Democratic leaders outline agenda after sweeping Congress in midterms The finger-pointing has already begun. One of the first casualties appears to be House Republican leadership. Speaker Mike Johnson has announced he will not seek another term as the party's leader in the House, guaranteeing a new face at the helm as Republicans attempt to regroup. Attention is also turning toward the White House and Trump's inner circle. Vice President JD Vance sparked discussion across Washington after publicly arguing that the party's losses were primarily tied to the conflict with Iran. WATCH: Pete Hegseth's future hangs in the balance Trump puts new scrutiny on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth In a social media post, Vance argued that the war was the central reason for the GOP's defeat and suggested any effort to rebuild the party must begin with an honest assessment of that decision. The comments have intensified scrutiny on senior administration officials, particularly Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Some Republicans are openly questioning whether changes at the Pentagon or elsewhere in the administration are necessary after the election results. The debate echoes a familiar chapter in modern political history. Following Republican losses in the 2006 midterm elections, President George W. Bush replaced Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld amid growing criticism over the Iraq War. Some Republicans are drawing parallels between that election and the party's current predicament. entry.title: Martin County flooding leaves cattle farmers struggling, residents demanding solutions - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County flooding leaves cattle farmers struggling, residents demanding solutions    WPBF
entry.article_text: Floodwaters continue to inundate properties in Martin County, leaving cattle farmers struggling to care for their animals and residents concerned about how much longer the water will remain. Residents in the Trailside community say water from neighboring properties is flowing into their drainage system, causing widespread flooding. Flooding threatens cattle, farm operations Hungryland Farms normally operates a 20-acre rotational grazing system for its Florida Cracker cattle. The owner, Melissa, said much of the pasture is now underwater, forcing the animals onto the farm’s elevated driveway. "We're starting to lose big sections of the driveway. We have them concentrated up the house pad, but if we lose too much more, we're just going to have to figure out a way to evacuate them somewhere," she said. Some cattle have struggled to navigate the water, and Melissa said the farm is concerned about losing access to its property as flooding continues. For now, the farm is bringing in hay and hay cubes to keep the cattle on their regular diet while monitoring potential health risks from floodwaters. "We’re more just concerned with the health and safety of our cattle," Melissa said. Melissa said the farm has an emergency contact with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service if the animals face imminent danger. "We don’t know how long we’re going to be here," she said. HOA says solution is unclear Kyla Shay, president of the Trailside Homeowners Association, said the community’s drainage system is designed to handle water from its 41 lots and designated neighboring properties. However, Shay said water from outside that system is now flowing through county-owned land and other neighboring properties before reaching the community’s southern canal. We can’t handle theirs," Shay said. The flooding has also affected neighboring pastures and reached areas near Bridge Road and an electrical substation, according to Shay. She said some electrical transformers are partially underwater, septic systems are overwhelmed and residents have been warned their well water could be compromised. "The health department issued warnings this morning to me that our water wells could be compromised because of bacteria, because of the standing water," Shay said. Since their septic systems are submerged, Shay said homeowners have been unable to shower or do laundry. County says repairs must wait WPBF 25 News reached out to Martin County about their concerns and learned the county recently acquired approximately 315 acres of land in the area, known as the Elise J. A county spokesperson said establishing access has been their immediate priority so staff can assess conditions and respond. The county said it is working with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District to address a breach affecting drainage into its irrigation canal and that the agencies jointly determined repairs should wait until water levels recede. The county said current conditions make hauling and placing sand unsafe and potentially damaging to the levee. Material could also wash into the canal before crews establish a stable repair. "County staff will continue to monitor water levels and site conditions in close coordination with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District," a county spokesperson said. The county said it will move forward with repairs when conditions allow safe work without compromising the levee. It is also evaluating longer-term options to improve outflow and reduce the risk of flooding happening again. Residents want a long-term solution Shay said the homeowners association has been working with water engineers and other experts to understand how long the flooding could last. "It's probably going to be late January, February before we can see a break, and that's assuming that the south canal wall does not collapse and immediately dump all the water on us," she said. Melissa said the farm’s drainage system normally provides room for water to collect during the rainy season, but the amount coming from outside the property has overwhelmed it. "We have a very extensive drainage system, but it’s just not equipped to handle this amount of water," Melissa said. Both women said they want neighboring properties and the agencies responsible for drainage to address the problem. For now, Martin County said it will continue monitoring conditions and coordinating with the conservancy district before attempting repairs. Meanwhile, Melissa said the farm is focused on keeping its cattle safe as water continues to surround the property.

entry.title: St. Lucie County flips blue after 14 years as voters increase turnout despite floods - WPEC
entry.summary: St. Lucie County flips blue after 14 years as voters increase turnout despite floods    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie County flipped blue in Tuesday's governor's race for the first time in more than a decade, as voter turnout climbed despite historic flooding that forced last-minute polling place changes. Democrat David Jolly carried the county with approximately 51% of the vote , compared with 48% for Republican Byron Donalds. The result marked the first time since 2012 that a Democratic candidate for governor or president won a majority in St. That year, former President Barack Obama carried the county with 53.42% of the vote. According to TCPalm , voter turnout reached 56.5% in the county, up 5.2 percentage points from the 2022 general election , when 51.3% of registered voters cast ballots. Lucie County ranked 51st among Florida's 67 counties, with only 16 counties reporting lower turnout. In 2022, the county had 238,645 registered voters, with 122,361 casting ballots. See also: Neighborhoods in Jensen Beach go underwater as flooding devastates the Treasure Coast Voters turn out despite historic flooding The increase came as widespread flooding forced election officials to relocate several polling places across Port St. Lucie, Tradition and Fort Pierce, per CBS12 reports . Lucie County Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker said the changes were necessary to ensure voters had safe and accessible locations to cast their ballots. Voters assigned to Oak Hammock K-8 School, Centennial High School and the Paula A. Lewis Library were among those affected, with some redirected to the Port St. Lucie Community Center, Indian River State College's Veterans Center of Excellence and Tradition Town Hall. The changes followed heavy rainfall that submerged roads, stranded vehicles and prompted evacuations across parts of the county. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for St. Lucie County and six other Florida counties, while flooding forced local public schools to close Tuesday and Wednesday. Despite the weather-related challenges, St. Lucie County surpassed its 2022 general election turnout rate while delivering a Democratic majority in the governor's race for the first time in 14 years, when Obama won the county. While the flooding complicated Election Day logistics, the higher turnout suggests those challenges did not prevent overall participation from exceeding the previous gubernatorial election.

entry.article_text: Much of a Jensen Beach neighborhood on Hyline Drive is underwater after this week's heavy rain overwhelmed the local drainage system. As of Wednesday afternoon, water levels inside some homes are still rising long after the rain stopped.For Lisa French and Tiffany Kincaid, a kayak has become the way to get around their flooded community.WATCH REPORT BELOW: At Kincaid's home, the water level is waist-deep."We're currently taking stuff out of our house right now, salvaging what we can," said Kincaid.At French's home, the damage has just begun, with the water level climbing to 4 inches deep."My floorboards are outside, but it's still rising. My husband made a mark inside so it's still coming up and ours isn't nearly as bad as everyone else," French said.Their homes are among dozens in the neighborhood under water after Monday's heavy rain saturated the ground and inundated the drainage system."We were expecting flooding to go down. Clearly drainage is not — things are not draining correctly," Kincaid said.Martin County told us the neighborhood is uniquely located next to the Savannas Preserve, where water is naturally flowing south from other areas that flooded. For now, the county says it's unable to pump water out of the community because the nearby watershed doesn't have capacity, but relief may be on the horizon."As the water level drops, that's going to drain the ponds that we need to pump into, and that's going to allow us to do that," Martin County's Public Works Director Jim Gordon said. "We're maximizing what we can downstream, and we might see it trending in the right direction."Residents are hoping relief comes sooner rather than later so they can start the long road to recovery."Even after, like, our houses are wrecked," French said."It's just a lot to take in right now for us," Kincaid said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: 23rd Street gang investigation leads to nearly 40 arrests in St. Lucie County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A nearly two-year investigation into the 23rd Street gang has led to nearly 40 arrests and the seizure of guns, drugs and cash, law enforcement officials said Thursday. The multi-agency investigation, called Operation Score Board, focused on alleged gang activity in northwest Fort Pierce and surrounding areas. Officials said investigators linked 13 people to an alleged criminal conspiracy involving fraud, drug trafficking, shootings and homicides. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said investigators reviewed 10 years of criminal activity and connected people associated with the gang to nearly 100 shootings. Investigators also found that gang members allegedly kept a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, which inspired the operation’s name. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said local, state and federal agencies took part in the investigation. The sheriff’s office, F ort Pierce Police Department , ATF , FBI , DEA , Florida Department of Law Enforcement , U.S. Marshals Service and Homeland Security Investigations were among the participating agencies. "Hundreds of shootings over the last decade, violent crime terrorizing the north end of this county, and our community deserves better, and they're getting better because of the hard work of the men and women with the special investigation units that the chief mentioned, and our federal partners here," said Sheriff Richard Del Toro.
