According to the Justice Department, death records showed some of the purported patients had died before the dates they supposedly received medical care.The scheme ultimately defrauded medical lenders of approximately $2.3 million, according to prosecutors.Federal prosecutors said Tullis was also involved in a separate scheme targeting a pandemic-era federal relief program.Between April and August 2020, Tullis submitted at least nine fraudulent applications to the U.S. Small Business Administration's Economic Injury Disaster Loan program, according to the Justice Department.The applications sought a combined $696,860 and included false information about businesses' numbers of employees and revenue, prosecutors said.Tullis pleaded guilty July 21 to conspiracy to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft.Two co-defendants were previously sentenced in connection with the case.Taneika Nakia Pace, 50, of Hallandale Beach, who prosecutors said managed two of the sham clinics, was sentenced in September to six months in prison after pleading guilty to bank fraud.Junaque Nicole Tullis, 46, of Coral Springs, was sentenced in August to eight months in prison after pleading guilty to wire fraud in connection with fraudulent Economic Injury Disaster Loan applications.All three defendants were charged as part of the Justice Department's 2025 National Health Care Fraud Takedown.The FBI investigated the case.

entry.title: Stuart Air Show: What to know about traffic, parking and getting to Witham Field
entry.summary: The Stuart Air Show is preparing to take flight at Witham Field, bringing aircraft, crowds and heavier traffic to the Stuart area. The air show is celebrating its 37th year at Witham Field. Lee Potter with the Stuart Air Show said this year's event will feature the F-16 demo team along with a variety of other aircraft arriving throughout the week. For drivers, planning the route before leaving home can help make the trip easier. Getting to the Stuart Air Show Drivers coming from Interstate 95 can take the Stuart exit and use Kanner Highway to Monterey Road. Drivers using Florida's Turnpike can take Southwest Martin Downs Boulevard. U.S. 1 and Dixie Highway are also options for reaching Monterey Road. As drivers approach Witham Field, they should follow posted signs and directions from law enforcement. The air show has two drive-in entrances off Monterey Road, with the Martin County Sheriff's Office directing traffic in the area. Where to park General parking is free in designated Stuart Air Show parking areas. Complimentary shuttle service will take visitors from the parking areas to the main gates. ADA parking is also available. Drivers should not create their own parking spots or park outside the designated areas. The best advice: stick with the official parking lots, watch for posted signs and follow law enforcement directions as you approach the air show. WPTV Traffic Reporter Johann Hoffend will be at Witham Field with traffic and transportation information for people heading to the Stuart Air Show.

entry.title: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows - WPEC
entry.summary: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows    WPEC
entry.article_text: A woman who called 911 during a Palm City standoff told dispatchers a man was chasing her with guns and had fired them, according to the call transcript released through a public records request. Please, quickly, the woman said at the start of the call. She told the dispatcher she was running down the street and that the man was so drunk and had tried to get into a car. The call adds detail to the September standoff involving Darrel Abbey, which lasted several hours and brought Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, SWAT team members and hostage negotiators to the home. In an earlier report, investigators said Abbey allegedly threatened his ex-girlfriend and pointed a gun at her. The woman told the dispatcher Abbey had put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger about an hour and a half earlier. She said the gun did not fire and that he was not in a good state of mind. As she ran, the caller said Abbey turned around and headed back toward the home. She stopped on the side of the road, where she said another woman had pulled over to help her. The caller also told dispatchers there were multiple guns at the property, though she was unsure whether they were inside the house, in a vehicle or in an RV. Newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property during the response. The footage is partially obscured, and the provided clip does not clearly show Abbey or the events described in the 911 call. See also: 18-year-old dies after being struck by car in St. Lucie County; family raises concerns According to the arrest report, Abbey’s ex-girlfriend went to his home after their breakup. She told investigators he appeared intoxicated and had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts. The report says he brought the guns inside, yelled at her and pointed a gun at her several times. It also says he later tried to get into his vehicle and reached for her phone when he realized she was recording. She ran down the road and called 911. Deputies later tried to contact Abbey at the home, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, according to the arrest report. He was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. The report also identifies him as a convicted felon with a prior vehicular assault conviction in Washington state.

entry.title: Tampa father jailed in Florida voter sweep as attorney questions state's evidence against him
entry.summary: A Tampa father accused of voting illegally is now behind bars one of 20 defendants charged with voter fraud as part of the state's latest sweep. But his attorney is questioning the state's evidence, telling investigative reporter Katie LaGrone she hasn't seen proof of her client's wrongdoing beyond a voter card the state sent him even though he was ineligible to vote. WATCH KATIE LAGRONE'S REPORT BELOW: Attorney questions Tampa father's voter fraud case In a Hillsborough County courtroom recently, Donta White sat in the inmate section, dressed in an orange jumpsuit, his expression stoic. This court appearance was about scheduling his trial, but for the people waiting for the 44-year-old to return home, the consequences of his latest arrest have already settled in. 'I thought it was a prank. Like, what do you mean? There's officers here to arrest you for voting? He's like, 'I didn't do it,'' said Taquilla Allen, White's girlfriend. She's helping to care for his two young children while he remains in jail. 'It's been rough, but you know, we're just gonna take it a day at a time,' Allen said. The state is accusing White of illegally voting. At the time, the convicted felon was still serving a 10-year probation for grand theft when, according to a press release issued by Florida's Attorney General's Office, White signed a state form warning him not to register or vote until after he completed his sentence. But according to prosecutors, White submitted two voter registration applications falsely claiming his voting rights had been restored, and then voted early in the 2024 general election. White is now charged with illegal voting and two counts of false swearing. A spokesperson for the AG's office said White admitted to authorities that he registered and voted, but his attorney, Lynley Flagler, is questioning the state's case. 'There is no clear-cut evidence that would support the fact that he actually went to the polls and voted himself,' Flagler said. In addition, despite White not being eligible to vote because of his felony conviction, Flagler says the state sent him a voter ID card as if he was eligible. entry.article_text: A Tampa father accused of voting illegally is now behind bars — one of 20 defendants charged with voter fraud as part of the state's latest sweep. But his attorney is questioning the state's evidence, telling investigative reporter Katie LaGrone she hasn't seen proof of her client's wrongdoing beyond a voter card the state sent him even though he was ineligible to vote.WATCH KATIE LAGRONE'S REPORT BELOW: In a Hillsborough County courtroom recently, Donta White sat in the inmate section, dressed in an orange jumpsuit, his expression stoic. This court appearance was about scheduling his trial, but for the people waiting for the 44-year-old to return home, the consequences of his latest arrest have already settled in."I thought it was a prank. There's officers here to arrest you for voting? He's like, 'I didn't do it,'" said Taquilla Allen, White's girlfriend. She's helping to care for his two young children while he remains in jail."It's been rough, but you know, we're just gonna take it a day at a time," Allen said.The state is accusing White of illegally voting. At the time, the convicted felon was still serving a 10-year probation for grand theft when, according to a press release issued by Florida's Attorney General's Office, White signed a state form warning him not to register or vote until after he completed his sentence.But according to prosecutors, White submitted two voter registration applications falsely claiming his voting rights had been restored, and then voted early in the 2024 general election. White is now charged with illegal voting and two counts of false swearing.A spokesperson for the AG's office said White admitted to authorities that he registered and voted, but his attorney, Lynley Flagler, is questioning the state's case."There is no clear-cut evidence that would support the fact that he actually went to the polls and voted himself," Flagler said.In addition, despite White not being eligible to vote because of his felony conviction, Flagler says the state sent him a voter ID card as if he was eligible."I feel that there's an entrapment issue. They want to prosecute voting, but they have not put any checks and balances in place to let people know when they're able to vote and when they can't vote," Flagler said.While a voter ID card does not, by itself, grant someone the right to vote, under Florida law certain convicted felons can get their voting rights restored once they complete their sentence, including probation. In White's case, his illegal voting charges triggered a violation of probation, which is how he landed back in jail."He runs a body shop. He's just, overall, really changed his life. So to see him in this position saddens me on a personal level as well as a professional level," Flagler said.Questions around voter eligibility for convicted felons aren't new in Florida. Ron DeSantis announced the arrests of 20 former felons who cast a ballot despite having disqualifying convictions. Several said they thought they could vote."What we discovered from a review of all those cases was there was more confusion than fraud," said Ramon De La Cabada, a Florida criminal defense attorney who co-chairs a committee formed after those arrests.De La Cabada believes White's case may be another example of that confusion — as is the recent arrest of Astrid Navarette Quintana. She's sitting in a Lee County jail after the state charged her for voting as a non-citizen. LaGrone recently investigated her case and found she's a permanent resident, married to a U.S. veteran and was also sent a voter ID card. When asked why voters shouldn't be responsible for knowing if they're eligible to vote, De La Cabada responded, "Absolutely, but I think the better question is why isn't the government creating better communication about eligibility? What you're finding in all these cases is massive confusion as to eligibility."Donta White's jury trial is set for early next year. He faces up to 15 years in prison for illegally voting and 30 years for his probation violation, which stemmed from his recent voting charges.In the meantime, he and his family remain apart, waiting for what's next."Who would throw their life away to vote? That's what it all boils down to," his girlfriend said. "It's petty, but we're dealing with it."

entry.title: Military Trail reopens in both directions after repairs following deadly Learjet crash
entry.summary: Military Trail reopened Thursday night in both directions near Greenacres after crews completed roadway repairs following the fatal Learjet crash on Nov. 1, according to the Florida Department of Transportation. FDOT said two northbound and two southbound lanes opened to drivers as of 7:05 p.m. Thursday. Crews spent the past 48 hours repairing the roadway, including paving and striping the road. Sidewalk repairs also began Thursday. Earlier Thursday, FDOT said crews had worked overnight and into Thursday morning to reopen the northbound lanes. This area of Military Trail had been closed between 10th Avenue and Forest Hill Boulevard after the Learjet crash created a large crater in the road. The reopening restores traffic in both directions along the affected stretch of Military Trail. Nine people were killed when the Learjet, which departed Austin, Texas, en route to the Bahamas, crashed near Greenacres earlier this month. No one on the ground was seriously injured.

entry.title: FHP trooper-involved shooting incident shuts down I-95 in Indian River County
entry.summary: Interstate 95 in Indian River County was shut down in both directions early Friday morning, creating a major traffic disruption for drivers near the Indian River-St. Lucie County line. On Thursday, at about 11:20 p.m., FHP said a trooper was involved in a shooting incident on I-95 near mile marker 141. According to FHP, the incident began when the trooper initiated a traffic stop, and the suspect fled, resulting in a pursuit. The pursuit escalated and turned into a gunfire exchange between the trooper and the suspect. Authorities said no troopers were injured during the shooting. FHP said the suspect sustained injuries from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound and was pronounced dead at the scene. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said the highway is closed due to the ongoing investigation. All northbound and southbound lanes of I-95 are closed at this time. The southbound entrance ramp at Oslo Road is also shut down. Northbound drivers were being directed off I-95 at Indrio Road, while southbound drivers were being directed to exit at Oslo Road. The northbound entrance ramp from Indrio Road is also closed. Officials said all body cam and dash cam video will be reviewed during the investigation. The FDLE will take over as the lead on the investigation. WPTV is working to learn more about when the interstate could reopen.

entry.title: Riviera Beach's Lone Pine community faces devastation after historic flooding
entry.summary: Residents of Riviera Beach's Lone Pine community are confronting the aftermath of devastating flooding, with gutted homes, piles of belongings lining neighborhood streets and families struggling to figure out what comes next. A week after floodwaters forced residents from their homes, the damage is becoming clearer, leaving some without flood insurance and questioning whether they can afford to rebuild. The flooding has turned once-familiar homes into cleanup projects and left residents facing the loss of belongings, memories and, in some cases, their sense of security. WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman returned to Lone Pine after witnessing the flooding begin to speak with residents now trying to recover. Watch report from Michael Hoffman: Riviera Beach's Lone Pine community faces devastation after historic flooding 81-year-old resident loses everything in flooding For 81-year-old Hazeline Thomas, the damage is deeply personal. Thomas walked Hoffman through her damaged home, where much of her belongings had been removed and left in piles along the curb. 'I'm all alone. And all my life saving is on the sidewalk,' Thomas said. She described being trapped inside her home as floodwaters rose around her. Thomas said the water eventually reached her neck before firefighters rescued her by boat. 'The water was up to my neck,' Thomas said. 'So the firefighters, the men, had to pick me up and put me in the boat.' She said rescuers also helped evacuate neighbors across the street. Now, Thomas is facing the financial burden of cleaning out her home. She said she has had to pay people to remove damaged belongings, using money she can hardly afford to spend. 'Everybody's just stuck, and we have to be doing things on our own,' Thomas said. With her home destroyed and few resources available, Thomas said she is considering leaving Florida and returning to New York. 'What I really need to do is pack up and go back to New York,' she said. So, where do I go from here?" she asked.Without flood insurance, Thomas faces uncertainty about how she will pay for repairs, replace her belongings, or find a place to live.Her situation highlights the challenges facing homeowners in Lone Pine as the community begins the long cleanup process.For residents like Thomas, the immediate concern is getting through the cleanup. But the bigger question is whether they will have the financial resources to put their lives back together.In Lone Pine, the floodwaters have receded. The questions left behind are only beginning.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. "It's completely covered," Melissa said. they're all underwater."The flooding has left her animals without their primary food source and exposed them to potentially deadly hazards, including drowning, waterborne parasites and electrical dangers.Melissa pointed to an electrical transformer nearly submerged by floodwater, questioning whether her cattle could be electrocuted if they wandered too close.And despite the rain stopping, she said the water isn't draining — it's rising. "We always thought we were through because the rain had stopped, but the water kept rising," she said.For Trailside Homeowners Association President Kyla Shay, the flooding is the culmination of years of unresolved drainage concerns.In a 2018 letter obtained by WPTV, Shay warned homeowners that property south of Trailside had effectively become a reservoir, with water rising as much as 3.5 feet above community roads and breaching a berm — a raised barrier designed to control water flow.That same year, Shay contacted the South Florida Water Management District, warning that blocked drainage had left some pastures under 8 feet of water.She asked for help but says the underlying problems were never resolved."It's a combination of years of 'We'll get to it,' and we never got to it," Shay said.Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton acknowledges the community faces significant drainage challenges.Gorton said a berm breached Monday on the county-owned Elise J Property northeast of Trailside, sending water into a nearby canal, with some water backflowing into the community."We still can't get back to that breach," Gorton told investigative reporter Kate Hussey, explaining that high water levels have prevented crews from accessing the area.But the larger problem, he said, is Trailside's geography.The community is essentially a bathtub, surrounded by berms, hundreds of acres of wetlands and two independent water control districts.Water flows into the area, but there is only one drainage ditch for it to slowly escape."There's no easy way to get that water out except by pump or gravity," Gorton said.WPTV contacted engineer Bob Higgins, who works with both the Pal Mar Water Control District and the Hobe St. Lucie Conservancy District.Higgins said a potential solution had already been designed years ago: an outfall that would allow water to drain through the R G Mitigation Bank Preserve to the south and the neighboring Elise J property, which Martin County acquired in 2026. But that project was never built.When Hussey asked Gorton whether the county had been aware of the proposal, he confirmed officials had discussed it with the property's former owner."We did have some dialogue with the previous owner of Elise J about creating a formal water control structure that could discharge before the berms would breach," Gorton said.According to Gorton, the former owners submitted two permit applications to the South Florida Water Management District, but construction never began.WPTV contacted the former property owners, who said they did not know why the project was never completed.When Hussey reached out to the South Florida Water Management District, the agency said Trailside was outside its jurisdiction.However, Gorton said the district had permitted every property within Trailside and oversaw the proposed drainage project.Hussey followed up with the district, seeking clarification about its jurisdiction and asking why the drainage project was never constructed.The district has not responded to those follow-up questions.Despite the years of delays, Gorton said there may finally be a path forward."The good news is the county purchased that property, and it's our intent to bring that project forward," he said.Gorton said he has already requested the original permit applications in hopes of expediting approval — and construction— of the project.He also plans to return Friday to assess the flooding and determine what immediate relief may be possible."We're looking at ways to get the water out faster," he said.But for residents like Melissa, every additional day underwater carries a cost. "This could be a very costly natural disaster for us," she said.Her cattle still need to eat. Their pastures are submerged. And with no clear timeline for when the water will recede, the future of her farm remains uncertain."I don't have any food," Melissa said to her cows. "I'm sorry."For now, Hungryland Farms is living up to its name — and the families who depend on it are waiting for the water to go down.WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey continues to seek answers from the South Florida Water Management District about the proposed drainage project and why it was never completed.

entry.title: St. Lucie County rejects plan that could bring nearly 500 homes to low-lying site - cw34.com
entry.summary: St. Lucie County rejects plan that could bring nearly 500 homes to low-lying site    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County commissioners voted 3-2 to reject a land-use change for a roughly 34-acre property near South 25th Street and West Midway Road that could allow nearly 500 homes. The vote came as residents sought answers about recent flooding and commissioners questioned how the property handles drainage. An engineer said the property receives drainage from about 134 acres and uses a 24-inch pipe to direct water to nearby canals. Another pipe might be needed. The property sits lower than surrounding roads and would need to be raised for development, prompting concerns that construction could push water onto nearby properties. If designated for residential use, the site could allow up to 15 homes per acre, according to the discussion. County staff recommended approving the land-use change with adjustments to avoid or reduce impacts to wetlands and required buffers. Commissioners denied the request. See also: 77 homes hit by Martin County flooding. Where to get help now At the same meeting, residents from Creekside and White City asked commissioners to investigate last week’s flooding, identify who is responsible for local drainage systems, and explain how to prevent future flooding. I love my community, but it’s not fair that we’re suffering because nobody has taken the initiative to do what’s right for us, one resident said. Creekside residents called for an engineering review of the neighborhood and surrounding watershed, a reassessment of flood risk and a mitigation plan with deadlines. They also asked for a public meeting with county engineers and stormwater officials. White City residents described recurring flooding and called for drainage improvements and more stormwater storage. One resident said her home and yard had flooded four times since 2012. The county also made its emergency declaration official after days of heavy rain and flooding. It covers hazards including flooded roads and strained drainage systems.

entry.title: Western St. Lucie County residents seek answers after historic flooding - WPTV
entry.summary: Western St. Lucie County residents seek answers after historic flooding    WPTV
entry.article_text: Residents and farmers in western St. Lucie County are seeking answers and long-term drainage solutions after historic flooding left homes, farms and roads underwater last week.The North St. Lucie River Water Control District held an emergency meeting Monday to hear concerns from people in the area, including farmers, residents and representatives from Save the Chimps. District members said the drainage system can handle only so much water during an extreme rainfall event and discussed engineering as part of a possible long-term plan.WATCH REPORT BELOW:Some of the hardest-hit areas are now seeing significant improvement, including Save the Chimps in western St. But residents and farmers say they want to know what can be done to reduce the risk of similar flooding during the next extreme rainfall event.For one resident, the flooding has already changed how they view their future in the area."I will be selling my house cause I am not going to risk my investment," the resident said during Monday's meeting.Water control district hears concerns from western St. Lucie River Water Control District held an emergency meeting Monday to hear from people affected by the flooding.Farmers, residents and representatives of Save the Chimps attended as district members discussed the drainage system and the scale of last week's flooding.President Steve Cassens said there are limits to what the existing system can handle when extraordinary amounts of rain fall in a short period."If we have a rainfall event like that, my personal feeling is you can have gates open, shut, it doesn't matter," said Cassens. "We can manage water maybe 3, 4, 5, 6 inches. We can't manage water in the quantities that we got."District officials also discussed maintaining waterways and ditches, including concerns about a creek in Western Fort Pierce that serves as a primary drainage route. The district said it systematically cleans ditches within its boundaries.The district said it could examine engineering as part of developing a long-range plan.Conditions improve at Save the ChimpsSave the Chimps, a sanctuary in western St. Lucie County, was among the places hit hard by the flooding.WPTV previously reported that staff members had to use drones to deliver food to chimpanzees because several roads through the sanctuary were underwater.When WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache returned days later, staff said conditions had significantly improved."A short 40 hours after that, we're almost completely dry on our roads," said Mark Yohannan.The improvement came after days of challenges caused by standing water at the sanctuary.West Fort Pierce farmer raises concernsThe concerns extended beyond residential neighborhoods.Justin Akerley, who helps operate Saint Lucie Farm Preserve in west Fort Pierce, spoke later Monday at a Port St. Lucie City Council meeting after attending the water control district meeting.Akerley told council members he believes continued development is adding pressure to the area's drainage infrastructure."I just spent my morning in a meeting with the North St. Lucie River Water Control District trying to figure out what we can do to alleviate the water issues, and there's really no right answer except for stop building," Akerley said.Akerley shared a video with WPTV showing flooding at Saint Lucie Farm Preserve, a working agritourism farm operated by Akerley and Michael Hale. The farm produces hay, cut flowers, beef and assorted vegetables and hosts community agricultural events.Akerley told council members the consequences extend to other farms and families."I've got friends that have calves dying that are flooded; they can't get out," he said. "It's a terrible, terrible situation for everybody. There's people that have lost their homes."He urged city leaders to reconsider the effect future development could have on flooding and drainage."Just please reconsider because it's not a good situation for everybody, and it's only gonna get worse," Akerley said.Officials consider what comes nextDuring Monday's Port St. Lucie City Council meeting, Councilman David Pickett also called for greater scrutiny of flooding and the city's stormwater infrastructure.Pickett said he sent two memos to the city manager earlier in the week addressing floodwaters and wants the city to expedite a planned stormwater study rather than wait until 2029.He also raised concerns about flooding in Tradition and called for the city to examine stormwater systems before distributing certain stormwater fees to community development districts.Meanwhile, the North St. Lucie River Water Control District has said engineering options can be assessed as officials consider a long-term plan.For residents and farmers still recovering from last week's flooding, those discussions are now turning toward a larger question: what can be done before the next extreme rainfall event?This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: South Florida families turn to resale shopping to save money as holiday season approaches
entry.summary: Shoppers were out at the South Florida Fairgrounds on Friday looking for bargains at a large resale event featuring children's items. 'I love the fact that I can save a lot of money, and I like the shopping experience,' said Tatiana, a shopper who drove from Port St. Lucie. WATCH REPORT BELOW: South Florida families turn to resale shopping to save The resale event is run by Just Between Friends Palm Beach, a consignment shop. Among the items for sale were tables of toys, racks of clothing and various accessories from playpens to bicycles and strollers. 'Everything here is brought in by local families that have gently used items that their kids have outgrown, and instead of throwing it away, they're able to come bring it here and help other families save on items,' says store owner Kim Hazim. Resale shops are growing in popularity as inflation strains family budgets, and Hazim said this event has grown over the years. 'We used to be in 15,000 square feet; now we're in 30,000 square feet because that's how many families really need to come out,' Hazim said. Many were getting an early jump on holiday shopping with Black Friday coming later this month, but deals are already out there. 'Black Friday is almost a month-long event,' says money-saving expert Andrea Woroch. 'Retailers like Best Buy, Nordstrom, even Sephora, they started rolling out doorbuster-like deals on Nov. 1.' She added that good deals are already out there. 'If you're seeing a good deal, and again, I think that 30% off benchmark is a great place to make a purchase at,' Woroch said. 'And keep in mind, some retailers will offer price adjustments within a week or two weeks.'

entry.title: Russian national pleads guilty in $7 million Palm Beach County Medicare fraud, laundering scheme
entry.summary: A Russian national pleaded guilty Friday to his role in a Medicare fraud scheme rooted in Palm Beach County, marking the first conviction in a case I first brought to you last year. In federal court, 29-year-old Nika Machutadze, with the help of a translator, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. He is one of the defendants linked to a fraudulent medical equipment company in Delray Beach called Sunshine Senior Solutions , and he admitted under oath to his involvement in a money laundering scheme totaling more than $7 million. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Russian national pleads guilty in $7 million Palm Beach County Medicare fraud Machutadze could face up to 20 years in prison, plus fines, restitution and deportation. Seniors first contacted me last year, sharing Medicare statements for medical equipment they didn't need or receive from Sunshine Senior Solutions. While I tallied up hundreds of thousands of dollars in false claims from the statements I reviewed, that was a drop in the bucket, according to federal prosecutors. Federal prosecutors say Sunshine Senior Solutions billed insurers for more than $3 billion, though only a fraction of that was paid out. Machutadze admitted to opening bank accounts for Sunshine Senior Solutions and a second similar business in Texas, and transferring some of the money paid by insurers overseas. I reached out to some of the seniors to share the news of the guilty plea. 'Oh, that's terrific,' said Laura Carmine, of Illinois. 'Nice to know that justice can be done.' 'I'm glad to hear that,' said Mike Parrett, of Ohio. I spoke with Machutadze's attorney, Tony Mirvis, after Friday's hearing. 'The government's evidence was overwhelming,' Mirvis said. Mirvis said his client thought he was just taking a job. 'What I think is important is he's like the tip of the spear,' Mirvis said. entry.title: Democrat Eileen Laubacher flips Colorado House seat, ousting Lauren Boebert
entry.summary: Democrat Eileen Laubacher has defeated Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's 4th Congressional District, according to a race call by The Associated Press more than a week after Election Day. The race remained too close to call for days as election officials continued counting ballots. Laubacher's victory unseats one of President Donald Trump's most outspoken allies in Congress. Boebert has represented Colorado's 4th Congressional District since 2025. She previously represented the state's 3rd Congressional District but switched districts in late 2023, citing the need for a 'fresh start following a difficult year' that included family turmoil and several controversies. Laubacher, a retired Navy admiral who served in the military for more than 30 years, said her decision to run for Congress was driven by concerns about the country's future. 'I have never felt as much of a threat to our country, our Constitution, our very democracy, as I do at this time,' Laubacher said.

entry.title: Man dies in FHP trooper-involved shooting incident shuts down I-95 in Indian River County
entry.summary: Interstate 95 in Indian River County was shut down in both directions early Friday morning, creating a major traffic disruption for drivers near the Indian River-St. Lucie County line. WATCH: Lt. Indiana Miranda gives update after man dies in trooper-involved shooting incident FHP gives update on trooper-involved shooting incident On Thursday, at about 11:20 p.m., FHP said a trooper was involved in a shooting incident on I-95 near mile marker 141. According to FHP, the incident began when the trooper initiated a traffic stop for a man driving over 90 mph near mile marker 138. Another trooper joined as back up and that's when, FHP said, the man got aggressive and was uncooperative. 'The primary trooper who completed the stop addressed the driver and advised him the reason for the stop was the speed, asked him for his driver's license and registration, he noticed that the driver was hostile,' Lt. Indiana Miranda said during a press conference on Friday. 'There was a little bit of back and forth between the two, at which point the driver says, 'I don't want to talk to you,' and there was cursing by the driver to our primary trooper.' The second trooper stepped in, asking for the man's driver's license as well. That is when the man accelerated and fled the traffic stop, resulting in a pursuit. The pursuit escalated, when the suspect fired a gun at troopers, with one of the troopers returning fire. 'He said over the radio that there were shots being fired at them. Our trooper returned fire, while driving his vehicle and he was able to engage in a PIT,' Miranda said. FHP said the officers used a PIT maneuver causing the suspect to crash and rollover. Authorities said no troopers were injured during the shooting. The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene. FHP initially said the suspect sustained injuries from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. However, during the 2 p.m. press conference, FHP said that it is not clear who fired the shot that killed the suspect and that is under investigation. FHP said the Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating and the two FHP troopers are currently on paid administrative leave pending the outcome of the investigation. All northbound and southbound lanes of I-95 were closed for several hours into the morning. All lanes have since reopened.

entry.title: Martin County firefighters raise staffing concerns after it says hiring class canceled - cw34.com
entry.summary: Martin County firefighters raise staffing concerns after it says hiring class canceled    cw34.com
entry.article_text: The Martin County Firefighters Union is asking county leaders to reconsider canceling a firefighter hiring class planned for January, saying the department is already short-staffed and the loss of new hires could increase pressure on crews. In a Facebook post, the union said the county canceled the class, which was expected to bring about 25 firefighters into Martin County Fire Rescue . The county cited budget concerns tied to Amendment 3 , according to the union. The union said the department is 17 firefighters short now and could be about 25 short by January as employees retire or leave for other departments. Fewer firefighters mean fewer available personnel to respond to emergencies, increased reliance on mandatory and voluntary overtime, and greater demands placed on the firefighters who remain, the union wrote. The union said its members recently agreed to forgo negotiating a new contract that would have taken effect in October, giving up a cost-of-living pay adjustment to help the county address financial challenges. It said members did so after being assured that Fire Rescue would not be affected by hiring freezes tied to Amendment 3. See also: Bobcat rescued after getting caught in barbed-wire fence near Stuart The union also questioned county administrative pay increases, saying administrative employees received 6% raises in October while firefighters face staffing shortages. The post calls on the Board of County Commissioners and county administrator to move forward with the hiring class. The county was not quoted in the union’s post. Martin County is taking a measured approach to hiring as it evaluates its long-term financial outlook and operational needs. With rising operating costs, inflation, and potential revenue impacts following the passage of Amendment 3 and anticipated SAFER Grant repayment obligations in the upcoming budget cycle, the County is being mindful of additional staffing commitments. While the firefighter recruitment class was planned months before Amendment 3 passed, current fiscal considerations have prompted a review of future hiring. The County is currently taking a soft hiring freeze approach, carefully evaluating vacancies and staffing needs. Maintaining public safety remains a priority for Martin County," the County said in a statement.

entry.article_text: Interstate 95 reopened in both directions around noon Friday after a shooting involving a Florida Highway Patrol trooper shut down the highway near mile marker 141. "It's crazy, something you'd never see. You see it in the movies, but you would never expect gunshots," said Jason Thompson, a Port St. Thompson was on I-95 southbound Thursday night near Vero Beach and his 16 year old daughter was in the backseat when he says gunfire broke out between vehicles in the northbound lanes about 50 feet away. "It was a very dark stretch of highway right there and suddenly, crack, crack, crack! I saw the muzzle discharge. I scooted over a few lanes and just kind of hurried up and got away from the area," Thompson said. FHP said the incident began around 11:20 p.m. Thursday, when a trooper tried to stop a motorist for speeding. FHP says the driver was doing over 90 miles per hour. "The primary trooper who completed the stop addressed the driver and advised him the reason for the stop was his speed and asked him for his driver license, registration. He noticed that the driver was hostile during the time," said Lt. Indiana Miranda, FHP spokesperson. See also: FAA orders nationwide ground stop at all U.S. airports amid 'extraordinary circumstances' At that point there were two troopers at the traffic stop. Miranda says the driver would not provide his drivers license and sped away. "Both troopers entered their vehicles and they engaged in a pursuit. The primary trooper called out the locations as they were traveling northbound, the speed that he was traveling and subsequently he said over the radio that there were shots being fired at them. Our trooper returned fire while driving his vehicle. The subject engaged open fire to the officers as they were in an active pursuit and that's when the officers called it on the radio they were being shot at," Lt. One of the troopers performed a maneuver to stop the car about three miles from where the driver was first pulled over. The driver was found dead near his car. FHP was asked if the troopers in this incident followed proper policy. "In our policy there is different scenarios. Not every scenario can be picture perfect or fit just in a box. Our policy has to become flexible in the point that you have less than a second to even think or take action," Lt. The person’s name has not been released. FHP and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement are investigating. The road was closed for several hours overnight and again Friday morning while the investigation continued. FHP said any available dash camera or body-worn camera footage will not be released until authorized by the investigating agency. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: Fort Pierce mom demands answers after video shows moments before daughter’s death - cw34.com
entry.summary: Fort Pierce mom demands answers after video shows moments before daughter’s death    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A Fort Pierce mother is speaking out after watching body camera footage of the night her 19-year-old daughter was fatally shot in Fort Lauderdale near an Airbnb. She believes her daughter was asking police for help and wants to know whether the officers who first responded could have done more. I already knew half of what happened, and to see it and to hear it was heartbreaking, said Alacia Ford-Barron, the mother of Myrah Zeigler. She shared the video with CBS12 News. The body camera video shows officers arriving after an altercation involving two groups of women inside the Airbnb. Officers tell everyone to leave. Ford-Barron says her daughter had been attacked and that belongings, including car keys, were taken. The group needed to retrieve those items from a nearby park. In the footage, Zeigler asks officers to walk with the group to get their belongings. One officer asks whether they have a way to get to the park. Zeigler responds that they can. Ford-Barron says she believed officers were going to help. Minutes later, gunfire erupts nearby. An officer reports that shots were fired two blocks away. Friends can be heard screaming as officers try to revive Zeigler. She later died at a nearby hospital. See also: FDOT reopens all lanes on SR 809 and Military Trail after deadly Learjet 60 crash I wanted to know why they didn't call backup. I wanted to know why she did not listen to my daughter when she was trying to explain to her and asking her to walk down to the park, Ford-Barron said. Larry Lamar Smith was later arrested in connection with Zeigler’s death. Ford-Barron says she appreciates the detectives’ work but still has questions about the initial police response. I have to be my daughter's voice. I know that if I shut down, who's going to speak for my daughter? CBS12 News did not receive a response from Fort Lauderdale Police before publication. Update : In a statement provided Friday, the department said it remains saddened by the loss of Myrah Zeigler and extends its condolences to her family and loved ones. Police said the lead detective has maintained regular communication with the family and encouraged any concerns about the handling of the case to be addressed directly with the department through its established complaint process. The department declined an interview, citing the active and ongoing investigation.

entry.title: Delays, cancellations mount at President Donald J. Trump International Airport amid nationwide ground stop
entry.summary: A nationwide ground stop prompted by air traffic control communications issues caused widespread flight disruptions Friday, with passengers across South Florida facing delays and cancellations. The Federal Aviation Administration issued the ground stop as officials investigated the communications problems affecting air traffic control. At President Donald J. Trump International Airport, departure boards showed numerous delays, with some flights being canceled as the disruption continued. One traveler told WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman that she and her husband had planned to fly to Atlanta for a weekend trip but were told they likely would not be leaving Friday night. 'They said it didn't look good,' she said, describing what her husband had been told by TSA. 'Probably not leaving tonight.' Although disappointed, she said their travel wasn't urgent. 'This (travel to Atlanta) was just for fun, so disappointing,' she said. 'You know, rather safe than sorry.' Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials had no indication at the time that a malicious act or hacking contributed to the communications issues. The FAA remained in the early stages of investigating the problem, and additional information about what caused the disruption and what was being done to resolve it was not immediately available.

There's the raptor on the roof, the colorful atmosphere and the roadside billboard known for its witty, sometimes controversial messages. "And he was a larger-than-life character. We were both notorious wise hats."Harry's connection to the bar went back even further.According to DeStout, Harry's father opened Harry's Banana Farm in 1954. took over in the early 1980s and helped transform it from a more family-oriented establishment into a late-night hangout."Harry's the one that made it that late-night kind of hip place to be because he was like, he was a cool guy," DeStout said.Inside the bar, DeStout said reminders of his longtime friend are everywhere.When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez asked how much of the bar reminded him of Harry, DeStout didn't hesitate."Well, how could, how could it not? The whole place is him," DeStout said."He's the one that decorated all the stuff," he added.DeStout said many of the items inside the bar were collected during Harry's travels, with pieces from places including Australia and China.Inside, the bar's walls are a collage of Harry's travels and adventures with treasures at every inch.Harry was also behind another unmistakable piece of the bar's personality: its roadside sign."He was the original sign guy," DeStout said. "Yeah, way back when he started a tradition."DeStout eventually took over the tradition of putting messages on the sign and said he shared Harry's sense of humor."He always enjoyed it too," DeStout said. "But like I said, he was the original guy who did the sign."Harry's health began declining years ago. DeStout said Harry suffered a stroke roughly 17 years ago that paralyzed one side of his body. He recovered before suffering another stroke that took away his voice."He's had numerous other medical problems over the years, and then he started having heart problems and things like that," DeStout said. "So it's, it's been a difficult bunch of years for him."Still, DeStout said Harry continued living his life, traveling and attending events despite those challenges."He still lived life, and he got around more than I did," DeStout said. "He'd go to Las Vegas to the Sphere and the Kravis Center to plays, and, he got out and about a lot more than I did."Since Harry's death, DeStout said he's repeatedly heard one question from customers and employees: What happens to Harry's Banana Farm now?His answer is simple."Nothing. We're gonna continue on like we always do," DeStout said. "I've had to answer that question 100 times in the last two days. It's gonna keep on being Harry's Banana Farm."DeStout said that longevity is notable as Lake Worth Beach and the surrounding area continue to change. He recalled a time when Harry's was one of several similar neighborhood bars along Dixie Highway."When Harry and I tended bar here together 40 years ago, there was 10 places like Harry's up and down Dixie, and they're all gone," DeStout said. "Harry's is the only one that survives, and not only survives but thrives."For the people closest to Harry, his legacy extends beyond the walls of his neighborhood bar.DeStout said roughly 30 years ago, Harry began dressing as Santa Claus and visiting Barton Elementary School to give wrapped gifts to underprivileged children."He started going to Barton Elementary School and handing out wrapped gifts to all the little kids, underprivileged kids," DeStout said.What started at one school grew to include four elementary schools and eventually became a nonprofit, Harry's Helping Hands."And I just thought when we had the idea of making a legitimate nonprofit, it'd be a great legacy to leave behind," DeStout said. And now, after 30 years, it's gangbusters."The effort is marking its 30th year of giving back to the Lake Worth Beach community."He'd be here for the Christmas party; he'd be proud of everybody here for everything that they've done," DeStout said. "We've come so far, for a little neighborhood bar, we've done quite an impact."For DeStout, giving back is part of the responsibility that comes with operating a successful community business."And I believe, you know, very strongly that when, when you do business in the community, you profit from the community, you have a responsibility and obligation to contribute to that community, you know, so that's, and that was always Harry," DeStout said. "Harry was just so generous."DeStout is now encouraging people who want to honor Harry to donate to Harry's Helping Hands in lieu of flowers."He would much prefer a donation because that goes directly to the kids," DeStout said.Customers have also been stopping by Harry's Banana Farm to remember the man behind the business."He was very sarcastic, funny. He not only gave back, but he was a contributor, an active contributor," said Billy Miller, a patron at Harry's Banana Farm. "I would say he's going to be missed, absolutely."Hart shared a similar sentiment."It's definitely a bummer any time you hear a local person like that passes away, hopefully they're able to keep things going," Hart said.Everything DeStout says suggests that is exactly what they intend to do."This whole place is his legacy," DeStout said.And when Lopez asked what he would say to his longtime friend now, DeStout's answer brought that legacy back to where it started."I'll miss you, pal, but we're just gonna keep rolling along, just like we always have," DeStout said.A celebration of life for Harry Seifert Jr. 6 at the Lake Worth Beach Golf Club.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Russian national pleads guilty in $7 million Palm Beach County Medicare fraud, laundering scheme
entry.summary: A Russian national pleaded guilty Friday to his role in a Medicare fraud scheme rooted in Palm Beach County, marking the first conviction in a case I first brought to you last year. In federal court, 29-year-old Nika Machutadze, with the help of a translator, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. He is one of the defendants linked to a fraudulent medical equipment company in Delray Beach called Sunshine Senior Solutions , and he admitted under oath to his involvement in a money laundering scheme totaling more than $7 million. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Russian national pleads guilty in $7 million Palm Beach County Medicare fraud Machutadze could face up to 20 years in prison, plus fines, restitution and deportation. Seniors first contacted me last year, sharing Medicare statements for medical equipment they didn't need or receive from Sunshine Senior Solutions. While I tallied up hundreds of thousands of dollars in false claims from the statements I reviewed, that was a drop in the bucket, according to federal prosecutors. Federal prosecutors say Sunshine Senior Solutions billed insurers for more than $3 billion, though only a fraction of that was paid out. Machutadze admitted to opening bank accounts for Sunshine Senior Solutions and a second similar business in Texas, and transferring some of the money paid by insurers overseas. I reached out to some of the seniors to share the news of the guilty plea. 'Oh, that's terrific,' said Laura Carmine, of Illinois. 'Nice to know that justice can be done.' 'I'm glad to hear that,' said Mike Parrett, of Ohio. I spoke with Machutadze's attorney, Tony Mirvis, after Friday's hearing. 'The government's evidence was overwhelming,' Mirvis said. Mirvis said his client thought he was just taking a job. 'What I think is important is he's like the tip of the spear,' Mirvis said. 'I hate to say it, but he's kind of like a victim because the people that got him to work they're the ones that are making the millions of dollars, and he's making like literally nothing. He's getting in trouble for it.' Information filed in Friday's case mentions another defendant, Ibrahim Hilmi, and a second, unnamed co-conspirator. Hilmi, who is also tied to Sunshine Senior Solutions, is scheduled for trial in February. entry.title: Florida releases full list of 20 charged in voter fraud sweep; some arrests spark questions
entry.summary: Nearly seven weeks after announcing a statewide voter fraud sweep, Florida's attorney general has released the full list of people charged and some of the arrests have already raised questions. When Attorney General James Uthmeier announced the sweep on illegal voting in September, just before the midterm elections, his office named 12 of the 20 people charged. After repeated requests, a spokesperson from his office sent investigative reporter Katie LaGrone the full list this week. The 20 defendants span across 13 counties. They include four convicted felons and 16 non-citizens all of whom, according to the attorney general's office, were ineligible to vote at the time they are accused of casting a ballot. WATCH KATIE LAGRONE'S REPORT BELOW: DEFENDANTS NAMED IN VOTER FRAUD CASES But over the past few weeks, LaGrone has discovered some of these cases are raising questions. Among them is Astrid Quintana, a lawful permanent resident who had been in the country since she was a toddler and is married to a U.S. veteran. Her attorney told us she received a voter ID card before she voted in 2024, believing she could. 'She had no intention to deceive anybody or to do anything that she believed was illegal,' attorney Connor Martin said. In her Quintana's case and in at least seven other cases involving non-citizens now facing these charges LaGrone discovered the state citing a law that didn't even exist at the time they were accused of voting . When asked how the state could charge her over a law that didn't exist at the time of her alleged crime, Martin responded, 'Well, they cannot.' In response to LaGrone's findings, a spokesperson for the attorney general said those investigations are still pending. In Tampa, LaGrone recently caught up with the attorney for Donta White , a convicted felon who is not eligible to vote because he's still on probation for grand theft. entry.title: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue    WPBF
entry.article_text: A day after the firefighters' union in Martin County expressed concerns about staffing, the County Administrator is responding by acknowledging the concerns while also saying there's not much that can be done right now. The union raised its concerns in a Thursday social media post, pointing out that the county had canceled an upcoming hiring class of 25 new firefighters even as Fire Rescue is understaffed. "It is about public safety, firefighter working conditions, and ensuring Martin County residents receive the level of emergency services they pay for and deserve," the post said. Don Donaldson, the county administrator for Martin County, acknowledged the union's concerns. "I think the concern of the public is real and legitimate," Donaldson said. Donaldson confirmed that fire rescue is already short-staffed by 17 firefighters and that the hiring class will not proceed as planned. However, he clarified that the class is postponed, not canceled. "I don't want to have to lay somebody off six months right after I hire them," Donaldson said. He explained that the delay is due to uncertainties in the county budget caused by Amendment 3, a measure recently approved by Florida voters that will lower property taxes statewide. Martin County estimates the amendment will result in a $75 million revenue loss over the next two years. Donaldson emphasized the need to assess the budget before committing to new hires. "What I didn't want to have happen is to fully fund all of our firefighters and then find we have to eliminate a position or two with somebody already in the position," Donaldson said. Donaldson said he hopes to have more clarification on the hiring of firefighters within the next few months. Martin County Fire Rescue states the crash happened just before 11 a.m. on Friday near the 137 mile-marker in Palm City. entry.title: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows - WPEC
entry.summary: 911 caller said Palm City man was chasing her with guns, newly released video shows    WPEC
entry.article_text: A woman who called 911 during a Palm City standoff told dispatchers a man was chasing her with guns and had fired them, according to the call transcript released through a public records request. Please, quickly, the woman said at the start of the call. She told the dispatcher she was running down the street and that the man was so drunk and had tried to get into a car. The call adds detail to the September standoff involving Darrel Abbey, which lasted several hours and brought Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, SWAT team members and hostage negotiators to the home. In an earlier report, investigators said Abbey allegedly threatened his ex-girlfriend and pointed a gun at her. The woman told the dispatcher Abbey had put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger about an hour and a half earlier. She said the gun did not fire and that he was not in a good state of mind. As she ran, the caller said Abbey turned around and headed back toward the home. She stopped on the side of the road, where she said another woman had pulled over to help her. The caller also told dispatchers there were multiple guns at the property, though she was unsure whether they were inside the house, in a vehicle or in an RV. Newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property during the response. The footage is partially obscured, and the provided clip does not clearly show Abbey or the events described in the 911 call. See also: 18-year-old dies after being struck by car in St. Lucie County; family raises concerns According to the arrest report, Abbey’s ex-girlfriend went to his home after their breakup. She told investigators he appeared intoxicated and had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts. The report says he brought the guns inside, yelled at her and pointed a gun at her several times. It also says he later tried to get into his vehicle and reached for her phone when he realized she was recording. She ran down the road and called 911. Deputies later tried to contact Abbey at the home, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, according to the arrest report. He was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. The report also identifies him as a convicted felon with a prior vehicular assault conviction in Washington state.

entry.article_text: An 18-year-old man was killed after being struck by a car while walking on North Boulevard in unincorporated St. Lucie County, according to a Florida Highway Patrol crash report. Omari Linzell Williams was walking west in the westbound lane near Lee Boulevard when a Chevrolet sedan traveling west struck him with its front right corner, the report said. The crash was reported at 6:45 p.m. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach, where he was pronounced dead at 9:54 p.m., according to the report. The 30-year-old driver, who is from Vero Beach, was not injured and cooperated with law enforcement, the report said. Neighbors came outside after hearing the crash and provided aid. The Traffic Homicide Investigation is ongoing, FHP said. The report does not say whether any citations have been issued. See also: 13 state attorneys general ask Supreme Court to uphold Florida's Stop WOKE Act Williams’ family said he was walking to a store on the same road where he lived. Relatives are seeking more information about the crash and raising concerns about pedestrian safety on North Boulevard. A candlelight vigil for Williams is scheduled for 6 p.m. 13, at Lakewood Park, 5990 Emerson Ave.

entry.title: Stuart Air Show: What to know about traffic, parking and getting to Witham Field
entry.summary: The Stuart Air Show is preparing to take flight at Witham Field, bringing aircraft, crowds and heavier traffic to the Stuart area. The air show is celebrating its 37th year at Witham Field. Lee Potter with the Stuart Air Show said this year's event will feature the F-16 demo team along with a variety of other aircraft arriving throughout the week. For drivers, planning the route before leaving home can help make the trip easier. Getting to the Stuart Air Show Drivers coming from Interstate 95 can take the Stuart exit and use Kanner Highway to Monterey Road. Drivers using Florida's Turnpike can take Southwest Martin Downs Boulevard. U.S. 1 and Dixie Highway are also options for reaching Monterey Road. As drivers approach Witham Field, they should follow posted signs and directions from law enforcement. The air show has two drive-in entrances off Monterey Road, with the Martin County Sheriff's Office directing traffic in the area. Where to park General parking is free in designated Stuart Air Show parking areas. Complimentary shuttle service will take visitors from the parking areas to the main gates. ADA parking is also available. Drivers should not create their own parking spots or park outside the designated areas. The best advice: stick with the official parking lots, watch for posted signs and follow law enforcement directions as you approach the air show. WPTV Traffic Reporter Johann Hoffend will be at Witham Field with traffic and transportation information for people heading to the Stuart Air Show.

entry.title: Man dies in FHP trooper-involved shooting incident shuts down I-95 in Indian River County
entry.summary: Interstate 95 in Indian River County was shut down in both directions early Friday morning, creating a major traffic disruption for drivers near the Indian River-St. Lucie County line. WATCH: Lt. Indiana Miranda gives update after man dies in trooper-involved shooting incident FHP gives update on trooper-involved shooting incident On Thursday, at about 11:20 p.m., FHP said a trooper was involved in a shooting incident on I-95 near mile marker 141. According to FHP, the incident began when the trooper initiated a traffic stop for a man driving over 90 mph near mile marker 138. Another trooper joined as back up and that's when, FHP said, the man got aggressive and was uncooperative. 'The primary trooper who completed the stop addressed the driver and advised him the reason for the stop was the speed, asked him for his driver's license and registration, he noticed that the driver was hostile,' Lt. Indiana Miranda said during a press conference on Friday. 'There was a little bit of back and forth between the two, at which point the driver says, 'I don't want to talk to you,' and there was cursing by the driver to our primary trooper.' The second trooper stepped in, asking for the man's driver's license as well. That is when the man accelerated and fled the traffic stop, resulting in a pursuit. The pursuit escalated, when the suspect fired a gun at troopers, with one of the troopers returning fire. 'He said over the radio that there were shots being fired at them. Our trooper returned fire, while driving his vehicle and he was able to engage in a PIT,' Miranda said. FHP said the officers used a PIT maneuver causing the suspect to crash and rollover. Authorities said no troopers were injured during the shooting. The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene. FHP initially said the suspect sustained injuries from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. However, during the 2 p.m. press conference, FHP said that it is not clear who fired the shot that killed the suspect and that is under investigation. FHP said the Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating and the two FHP troopers are currently on paid administrative leave pending the outcome of the investigation. All northbound and southbound lanes of I-95 were closed for several hours into the morning. All lanes have since reopened.

Another trooper joined as back up and that's when, FHP said, the man got aggressive and was uncooperative. "The primary trooper who completed the stop addressed the driver and advised him the reason for the stop was the speed, asked him for his driver's license and registration, he noticed that the driver was hostile," Lt. Indiana Miranda said during a press conference on Friday. "There was a little bit of back and forth between the two, at which point the driver says, 'I don't want to talk to you,' and there was cursing by the driver to our primary trooper."The second trooper stepped in, asking for the man's driver's license as well. That is when the man accelerated and fled the traffic stop, resulting in a pursuit. The pursuit escalated, when the suspect fired a gun at troopers, with one of the troopers returning fire."He said over the radio that there were shots being fired at them. Our trooper returned fire, while driving his vehicle and he was able to engage in a PIT," Miranda said.FHP said the officers used a PIT maneuver causing the suspect to crash and rollover. Authorities said no troopers were injured during the shooting. The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene. FHP initially said the suspect sustained injuries from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. However, during the 2 p.m. press conference, FHP said that it is not clear who fired the shot that killed the suspect and that is under investigation.FHP said the Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating and the two FHP troopers are currently on paid administrative leave pending the outcome of the investigation.All northbound and southbound lanes of I-95 were closed for several hours into the morning. All lanes have since reopened.

entry.summary: A new cheerleading team at Passionate Care Services (PCS) is giving adults with disabilities the opportunity to perform, build friendships and become active participants in community events throughout Palm Beach County. entry.title: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County firefighters express concerns over staffing levels at Fire Rescue    WPBF
entry.article_text: A day after the firefighters' union in Martin County expressed concerns about staffing, the County Administrator is responding by acknowledging the concerns while also saying there's not much that can be done right now. The union raised its concerns in a Thursday social media post, pointing out that the county had canceled an upcoming hiring class of 25 new firefighters even as Fire Rescue is understaffed. "It is about public safety, firefighter working conditions, and ensuring Martin County residents receive the level of emergency services they pay for and deserve," the post said. Don Donaldson, the county administrator for Martin County, acknowledged the union's concerns. "I think the concern of the public is real and legitimate," Donaldson said. Donaldson confirmed that fire rescue is already short-staffed by 17 firefighters and that the hiring class will not proceed as planned. However, he clarified that the class is postponed, not canceled. "I don't want to have to lay somebody off six months right after I hire them," Donaldson said. He explained that the delay is due to uncertainties in the county budget caused by Amendment 3, a measure recently approved by Florida voters that will lower property taxes statewide. Martin County estimates the amendment will result in a $75 million revenue loss over the next two years. Donaldson emphasized the need to assess the budget before committing to new hires. "What I didn't want to have happen is to fully fund all of our firefighters and then find we have to eliminate a position or two with somebody already in the position," Donaldson said. Donaldson said he hopes to have more clarification on the hiring of firefighters within the next few months. entry.article_text: A woman who called 911 during a Palm City standoff told dispatchers a man was chasing her with guns and had fired them, according to the call transcript released through a public records request. Please, quickly, the woman said at the start of the call. She told the dispatcher she was running down the street and that the man was so drunk and had tried to get into a car. The call adds detail to the September standoff involving Darrel Abbey, which lasted several hours and brought Martin County Sheriff’s Office deputies, SWAT team members and hostage negotiators to the home. In an earlier report, investigators said Abbey allegedly threatened his ex-girlfriend and pointed a gun at her. The woman told the dispatcher Abbey had put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger about an hour and a half earlier. She said the gun did not fire and that he was not in a good state of mind. As she ran, the caller said Abbey turned around and headed back toward the home. She stopped on the side of the road, where she said another woman had pulled over to help her. The caller also told dispatchers there were multiple guns at the property, though she was unsure whether they were inside the house, in a vehicle or in an RV. Newly released sheriff’s office video shows deputies and a tactical vehicle at the property during the response. The footage is partially obscured, and the provided clip does not clearly show Abbey or the events described in the 911 call. See also: 18-year-old dies after being struck by car in St. Lucie County; family raises concerns According to the arrest report, Abbey’s ex-girlfriend went to his home after their breakup. She told investigators he appeared intoxicated and had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts. The report says he brought the guns inside, yelled at her and pointed a gun at her several times. It also says he later tried to get into his vehicle and reached for her phone when he realized she was recording. She ran down the road and called 911. Deputies later tried to contact Abbey at the home, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, according to the arrest report. He was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. The report also identifies him as a convicted felon with a prior vehicular assault conviction in Washington state.

entry.summary: St. Lucie County rejects plan that could bring nearly 500 homes to low-lying site    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County commissioners voted 3-2 to reject a land-use change for a roughly 34-acre property near South 25th Street and West Midway Road that could allow nearly 500 homes. The vote came as residents sought answers about recent flooding and commissioners questioned how the property handles drainage. An engineer said the property receives drainage from about 134 acres and uses a 24-inch pipe to direct water to nearby canals. Another pipe might be needed. The property sits lower than surrounding roads and would need to be raised for development, prompting concerns that construction could push water onto nearby properties. If designated for residential use, the site could allow up to 15 homes per acre, according to the discussion. County staff recommended approving the land-use change with adjustments to avoid or reduce impacts to wetlands and required buffers. Commissioners denied the request. See also: 77 homes hit by Martin County flooding. Where to get help now At the same meeting, residents from Creekside and White City asked commissioners to investigate last week’s flooding, identify who is responsible for local drainage systems, and explain how to prevent future flooding. I love my community, but it’s not fair that we’re suffering because nobody has taken the initiative to do what’s right for us, one resident said. Creekside residents called for an engineering review of the neighborhood and surrounding watershed, a reassessment of flood risk and a mitigation plan with deadlines. They also asked for a public meeting with county engineers and stormwater officials. White City residents described recurring flooding and called for drainage improvements and more stormwater storage. One resident said her home and yard had flooded four times since 2012. The county also made its emergency declaration official after days of heavy rain and flooding. It covers hazards including flooded roads and strained drainage systems.

entry.article_text: Interstate 95 in Indian River County is shut down in both directions early Friday morning, creating a major traffic disruption for drivers near the Indian River-St. 12, around 11:20 p.m., FHP said a trooper was involved in a shooting incident on I-95 near mile marker 141. According to FHP, the incident began when the trooper initiated a traffic stop, and the suspect fled, resulting in a pursuit. The pursuit escalated and turned into a gunfire exchange between the trooper and the suspect. Authorities said no troopers were injured during the shooting. FHP said the suspect sustained injuries from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound and was pronounced dead at the scene. The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office said the highway is closed due to the ongoing investigation. All northbound and southbound lanes of I-95 are closed at this time. The southbound entrance ramp at Oslo Road is also shut down. Northbound drivers were being directed off I-95 at Indrio Road, while southbound drivers were being directed to exit at Oslo Road. The northbound entrance ramp from Indrio Road is also closed. Officials said all body cam and dash cam video will be reviewed during the investigation. The FDLE will take over as the lead on the investigation. WFLX is working to learn more about when the interstate could reopen.

entry.title: 3,000 walkers fill downtown West Palm Beach for Heart Walk
entry.summary: Thousands of people dressed in red filled downtown West Palm Beach for this years American Heart Association Heart Walk, taking steps to support a cause that touches many families across the community. About 3,000 people took part in the event, which brings together survivors, families and supporters to raise awareness about heart disease and stroke. WATCH: 3,000 walkers fill downtown West Palm Beach for Heart Walk 3,000 walkers fill downtown West Palm Beach for Heart Walk WPTV is a proud sponsor of the Heart Walk, and WPTVs Ashley Glass served as emcee for this years event. For some of the families walking, the mission is deeply personal. WPTVs Christy Waite has been connecting with the family of a young girl named Blake, whose health journey has included heart failure and multiple open-heart surgeries. Before Blake was born, her parents learned she had a heart condition that would lead to multiple heart surgeries. When Blake was just 14 months old, she became very sick. 'She was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, and that put her heart into heart failure, so she had to have open-heart surgery as soon as possible,' her mom, Devin Aubrey, said. Unfortunately, the surgery didn't work, and a few months later Blake had her second open-heart surgery. Doctors put in a mechanical valve to help her heart open and close. As Blake continues to grow, so does her heart, but not the valve. When she is a little older, she will need to have another surgery to fix it. Blake's family formed Team Blake to give back and raise money through the Heart Walk. This year, Team Blake raised $10,000, surpassing the amount the team raised last year. Team Blake wasnt the only one celebrating a fundraising milestone. This years Heart Walk raised more than $1.4 million, setting a new fundraising record. For the walkers who filled downtown West Palm Beach, each step represented a different story, from survivors celebrating how far theyve come to families walking in support of someone they love.

entry.title: Man dies after crashing into palm trees in Fort Pierce in I-95 police chase - WPBF
entry.summary: Man dies after crashing into palm trees in Fort Pierce in I-95 police chase    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 59-year-old DeLand man died when he crashed into palm trees off Interstate 95 after being pursued by Florida Highway Patrol troopers at a high rate of speed on Saturday morning in Fort Pierce. Southbound lanes of Interstate 95 at Mile Marker 128 were closed at 7:45 a.m. near Okeechobee Road, which is State Road 70. A 2020 Volvo S60 was traveling southbound three miles away at Mile Marker 141 at a high rate of speed, according to FHP. A trooper was stationary on the southbound side and clocked the vehicle at 101 miles per hour, FHP said. Troopers attempted to intercept the driver for the traffic violation, but he failed to stop and continued to travel southbound at a high rate of speed, maneuvering in and out of traffic and utilizing the paved shoulders. A trooper attempted a PIT maneuver (Precision Immobilization Technique), which was unsuccessful, north of State Road 70. The driver continued traveling south at a high rate of speed and entered the inside paved shoulder and continued into the grass median, FHP said. The vehicle struck several large palm trees with the left front/driver’s side compartment. He was ejected and was pronounced deceased at the scene, FHP said.
